sentences.zh: 月五星犯列舍經星變附見

translations.literal: Transgressions of the Moon and the Five Planets against the Lodges and Classical Stars; appended observations on anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: The Moon and the Five Planets Transgressing the Lodges and Classical Stars, with Supplementary Notes on Celestial Portents.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初四年三月癸卯，月犯心大星。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth Huangchu year of Emperor Wen of Wei, on the day guimao, the Moon transgressed the great star of the Heart [lodge].
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the third month of Huangchu 4 under Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi), the moon occulted Antares, the bright star of the Heart mansion.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「心為天王位，王者惡之。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The Heart is the seat of the Celestial King; the king finds it ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication reads: “The Heart asterism marks Heaven’s throne—sovereigns dread such a sign.”

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiashen, the Great White [Venus] was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiashen, Venus appeared in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 案劉向《五紀論》曰：「太白少陰，弱，不得專行，故以己未為界，不得經天而行。

translations.literal: Investigating [this], Liu Xiang’s “Treatise on the Five Regulators” says: “The Great White is Lesser Yin; being weak, it cannot travel alone; therefore with jiwei as the boundary, it must not cross the sky [by day].
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang’s *Treatise on the Five Regulators* explains that Venus, as Lesser Yin, is too weak to travel alone; south of the jiwei line it normally does not march across the entire vault of the sky in daylight.

sentences.zh: 經天則晝見，其占為兵喪，為不臣，為更王；

translations.literal: When it crosses the sky, then it is seen by day; its interpretation is military losses, disloyal subjects, and change of king;
translations.idiomatic: When it nevertheless spans the full arc of the sky, it shines by day; the reading is war and mourning, rebellion, and the replacement of the ruler.

translations.literal: strong states weaken, small states strengthen.
translations.idiomatic: Great powers decline while lesser ones gain strength.

sentences.zh: 」是時孫權受魏爵號，而稱兵距守。

translations.literal: At this time Sun Quan accepted titles from Wei, yet raised troops and held out on the defensive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had accepted Wei’s patent of nobility yet still mobilized armies and stood on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 其十二月丙子，月犯心大星。

translations.literal: That twelfth month, on the day bingzi, the Moon transgressed the great star of the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingzi, the moon again crossed Antares in the Heart.

translations.literal: The interpretation is the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: The diviners cited the same gloss as above.

sentences.zh: 五年十月乙卯，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, tenth month, on the day yimao, the Great White was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Huangchu 5, on yimao, Venus appeared in daylight.

translations.literal: The interpretation is the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication matched the foregoing.

sentences.zh: 又歲星入太微逆行，積百四十九日乃出。

translations.literal: Moreover the Year Star [Jupiter] entered the Supreme Palace enclosure and moved retrograde; it accumulated one hundred forty-nine days there before emerging.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter also entered the Supreme Palace and traced a retrograde arc, lingering one hundred forty-nine days before departing.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「五星入太微，從右入三十日以上，人主有大憂。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Five Planets enter the Supreme Palace, entering from the right and staying thirty days or more, the ruler has great sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss runs: “If the five planets enter the Supreme Palace from the right and remain upward of thirty days, the sovereign faces grave distress.”

translations.literal: Another saying: “An amnesty will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: A variant reading adds: “A general amnesty is coming.”

sentences.zh: 」七年五月，帝崩，明帝即位，大赦天下。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year the emperor died; Emperor Ming succeeded and proclaimed a great amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year the emperor died; Emperor Ming took the throne and issued an empire-wide amnesty.

sentences.zh: 六年五月壬戌，熒惑入太微，至壬申，興歲星相及，俱犯右執法，至癸酉乃出。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, fifth month, on the day renxu, Spark-Delight [Mars] entered the Supreme Palace; by renshen it came together with the Year Star [Jupiter], both transgressing the Right Enforcer; on guiyou they emerged.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the fifth month of the sixth year Mars entered the Supreme Palace; by renshen it had closed with Jupiter, both crossing the Right Enforcer asterism, and they exited on guiyou.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「從右入三十日以上，人主有大憂。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Entering from the right and staying thirty days or more, the ruler has great sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation states: “Remaining from the right beyond thirty days brings great sorrow to the sovereign.”

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「月、五星犯左右執法，大臣有憂。

translations.literal: It also says: “When the Moon or the Five Planets transgress the Left or Right Enforcer, great ministers have sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Another clause warns that transits of the Left or Right Enforcer by the moon or planets foretell grief for chief ministers.

translations.literal: Another saying: “The enforcers are executed; metal and fire [planets] make it especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: A further gloss adds that “execution reaches the officials who ‘enforce the law,’ worst when Venus or Mars is involved.”

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the imperial son, Prince Jian of Dongwuyang, died.
translations.idiomatic: That November Prince Jian of Dongwuyang passed away.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，驃騎將軍曹洪免為庶人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year Cao Hong, General of Agile Cavalry, was dismissed and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month General of Agile Cavalry Cao Hong was stripped of rank and reduced to common status.

sentences.zh: 四月，征南大將軍夏侯尚薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Xiahou Shang, General Who Conquers the South, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Xiahou Shang, general who conquered the south, died.

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 《蜀記》稱明帝問黃權曰：「天下鼎立，何地為正？

translations.literal: The “Records of Shu” relates that Emperor Ming asked Huang Quan: “The realm stands tripod-wise—which region holds the true legitimacy?
translations.idiomatic: The *Records of Shu* records Emperor Ming asking Huang Quan which of the three rival courts possessed Heaven’s mandate.

translations.literal: He replied: “One must verify it against astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan answered that only celestial signs could settle the question.

sentences.zh: 往者熒惑守心而文帝崩，吳、蜀無事，此其徵也。

translations.literal: Formerly Spark-Delight stationed at the Heart and Emperor Wen died, yet Wu and Shu were untroubled—this was its proof.
translations.idiomatic: He cited how Mars had once ‘stationed at the Heart’ when Emperor Wen died while Wu and Shu remained unscathed—evidence, he claimed, of the omen’s bearing.

sentences.zh: 」案三國史並無熒惑守心之文，疑是入太微。

translations.literal: Investigating the histories of the three states, there is no text of Spark-Delight stationing at the Heart; it is suspected that [the planet] entered the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Scrutiny shows none of the Three Kingdoms annals records Mars ‘stationing at the Heart’; the event was probably entry into the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 八月，吳遂圍江夏，寇襄陽，大將軍宣帝救襄陽，斬吳將張霸等，兵喪更王之應也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Wu then besieged Jiangxia, raided Xiangyang, and Grand Marshal Xuandi relieved Xiangyang, beheading Wu generals including Zhang Ba—the response of military losses and change of ruler.
translations.idiomatic: That August Wu besieged Jiangxia and struck Xiangyang; Grand Marshal Xuandi (Sima Yi) rescued Xiangyang and slew Wu generals such as Zhang Ba, matching the omens of war, mourning, and shifting sovereignty.

sentences.zh: 明帝太和五年五月，熒惑犯房。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth Taihe year of Emperor Ming, Spark-Delight transgressed the Room [lodge].
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 under Emperor Ming, the fifth month, Mars crossed the Room mansion.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「房四星，股肱臣將相位也，月、五星犯守之，將相有憂。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The four stars of Room are the arms and legs—ministers and generals in council; when the Moon or the Five Planets invade or station there, generals and ministers will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss explains that Room’s four stars stand for the sovereign’s limbs—his commanding ministers; lunar or planetary trespass there promises grief for generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 」其七月，車騎將軍張郃追諸葛亮，為亮所害。

translations.literal: That seventh month General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang He pursued Zhuge Liang and was killed by Liang’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang He pursued Zhuge Liang and fell to Shu’s army.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.
translations.idiomatic: That December Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.

sentences.zh: 其十一月乙酉，月犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: That eleventh month, on yiyou, the Moon transgressed the great star of the Chariot Shaft [Regulus region].
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the eleventh month the moon crossed Regulus, the great star of the Chariot Shaft.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The principal consort will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The reading warns of peril to the chief lady of the palace.

sentences.zh: 」六年三月乙亥，月又犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, on yihai, the Moon again transgressed the great star of the Chariot Shaft.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the third month of the sixth year the moon repeated its transit across Regulus.

sentences.zh: 十一月寅，太白晝見南斗，遂歷八十餘日，恆見。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on the yin day, the Great White was seen in daytime in the Southern Dipper; it then lasted more than eighty days, constantly visible.
translations.idiomatic: On the yin day of the eleventh month Venus blazed by day within the Southern Dipper and remained visible more than eighty days running.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Wu will have soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication assigns armed conflict to the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 」明年，孫權遣張彌等將兵萬人，錫授公孫文懿為燕王，文懿斬彌等，虜其眾。

translations.literal: The next year Sun Quan sent Zhang Mi and others with ten thousand troops to invest Gongsun Wenyi as King of Yan; Wenyi executed Mi and seized his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Sun Quan dispatched Zhang Mi and others with ten thousand men to seal Gongsun Yuan as King of Yan; Yuan slew the envoys and impressed their troops.

sentences.zh: 青龍三年正月，太后郭氏崩。

translations.literal: In the first month of Qinglong 3, Empress Dowager Guo died.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 3’s first month Empress Dowager Guo passed away.

sentences.zh: 青龍三年三月辛卯，月犯輿鬼。

translations.literal: In the third month of Qinglong 3, on xinmao, the Moon transgressed the Ghosts [lodge].
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the third month of Qinglong 3 the moon crossed the Ghosts mansion.

translations.literal: The Ghosts govern beheading and killing.
translations.idiomatic: Astrologers assign executions and slaughter to the Ghosts asterism.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Many people fall ill; the state has sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss foretells widespread sickness and national mourning.

translations.literal: It also says: “Great ministers will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Another line warns that high ministers are imperiled.

translations.literal: That year, summer and winter, great pestilence [raged].
translations.idiomatic: Pestilence swept that summer and winter.

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year Minister of Education Dong Zhao died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year Minister of Education Dong Zhao died.

sentences.zh: 其五月丁亥，太白晝見，積三十餘日。

translations.literal: That fifth month, on dinghai, the Great White was seen in daytime, lasting more than thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai that fifth month Venus stayed visible in daylight for over thirty days.

sentences.zh: 以晷度推之，非秦魏，則楚也。

translations.literal: By gnomon-shadow reckoning of its position, [the omen applied] not to Qin or Wei, then to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Shadow-measurement placed the sign either with Qin-Wei or with the old Chu domain.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸葛亮據渭南，宣帝與相持；

translations.literal: At this time Zhuge Liang held the south bank of the Wei River while Xuandi confronted him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was entrenched south of the Wei as Xuandi faced him in stalemate;

sentences.zh: 孫權寇合肥，又遣陛議、孫韶等人淮沔，天子親東征。

translations.literal: Sun Quan raided Hefei and also sent Bi Yi, Sun Shao, and others into the Huai and Han rivers; the Son of Heaven campaigned east in person.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan struck at Hefei and dispatched Bi Yi, Sun Shao, and others along the Huai and Han; the emperor personally led the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 蜀本秦地，則為秦魏及楚兵悉起矣。

translations.literal: Shu was fundamentally the old Qin territory, so Qin, Wei, and Chu armies all rose together.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shu occupied the heartland of ancient Qin, the portent manifested as simultaneous campaigning across the Qin, Wei, and Chu theaters.

translations.literal: That seventh month, on jisi, the Moon transgressed Key-and-Bolt.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in the seventh month the moon crossed the Key-and-Bolt asterism.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be fire disasters.
translations.idiomatic: The reading predicts conflagration.

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year Chonghua Hall burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year Chonghua Hall caught fire.

sentences.zh: 三年六月丁未，填星犯井鉞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, on dingwei, the Station Star [Saturn] transgressed the Well’s Battle-Axe.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the sixth month of the third year Saturn crossed the battle-axe stars attached to the Well.

translations.literal: On wuxu the Great White again transgressed them.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Venus likewise crossed those stars.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「凡月、五星犯井鉞，悉為兵災。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Whenever the Moon or the Five Planets transgress the Well’s Battle-Axe, there are wholly military calamities.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss states that any lunar or planetary strike on the Well’s axe stars brings purely martial disaster.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Battle-axes are employed; great ministers are executed.
translations.idiomatic: A variant adds that axes of punishment appear and magnates face execution.

translations.literal: On jichou in the seventh month the Station Star transgressed the separator stars of the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou in the seventh month Saturn crossed the separator stars of the Eastern Well.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Station Star enters the Well, great men suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation warns that Saturn’s entry into the Well bodes ill for leading figures.

translations.literal: Moving close to the separator stars counts as traveling the ‘yin’ side.
translations.idiomatic: Passing near the separator stars is termed moving along the yin track.

translations.literal: Its interpretation says: “Great floods; the five grains do not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: That alignment promises inundation and crop failure.

translations.literal: In the summer of the first Jingchu year great floods damaged the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The summer of Jingchu 1 brought floods that ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 其年十月壬申，太白晝見，在尾，歷二百餘日，恆晝見。

translations.literal: That year, tenth month, on renshen, the Great White was seen in daytime in the Tail [lodge], lasting more than two hundred days, always visible in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen in the tenth month Venus shone by day in the Tail for over two hundred successive daylight apparitions.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The Tail is Yan; there will be soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss assigns Yan (the northeast) to the Tail and predicts warfare.

translations.literal: On wuchen in the twelfth month the Moon transgressed Hook-and-Hasp.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the twelfth month the moon crossed Hook-and-Hasp by the Heart.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The king will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The reading spells trouble for the ruler.

sentences.zh: 」四年閏正月己巳，填星犯井鉞。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the fourth year, on jisi, the Station Star transgressed the Well’s Battle-Axe.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in the intercalary first month of the fourth year Saturn again crossed the Well’s axe.

translations.literal: On guimao in the third month the Station Star transgressed the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the third month Saturn entered the Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 己巳，太白與月加景晝見。

translations.literal: On jisi the Great White together with the Moon “added radiance” [jiajing] and was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Venus and the Moon shone with compounded brilliance and were visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 五月壬寅，太白犯畢左股第一星。

translations.literal: On renyin in the fifth month the Great White transgressed the first star on the left thigh of the Net [Hyades].
translations.idiomatic: On renyin in the fifth month Venus crossed the first star on the Net’s left leg.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「畢為邊兵，又主刑罰。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The Net means border troops; it also governs punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss ties the Net to frontier armies and to penal justice.

sentences.zh: 」九月，涼州塞外胡阿畢師使侵犯諸國，西域校尉張就討之，斬首捕虜萬計。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Hu beyond the Liangzhou frontier, the envoy Abi Shi invaded the various states; Commandant of the Western Regions Zhang Jiu campaigned against them, beheading and capturing by the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn tribes beyond Liangzhou sent the envoy Abi Shi to raid the oasis kingdoms; Western Regions commandant Zhang Jiu crushed them, taking tens of thousands of heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 其年七月甲寅，太白犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: That seventh month, on jiayin, the Great White transgressed the great star of the Chariot Shaft.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the seventh month Venus crossed Regulus.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The principal consort will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The reading again signals peril to the empress.

translations.literal: In the first Jingchu year Empress Mao died.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 1 Empress Mao passed away.

sentences.zh: 景初元年二月乙酉，月犯房第二星。

translations.literal: On yiyou in the second month of Jingchu 1 the Moon transgressed the second star of the Room [lodge].
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the second month of Jingchu 1 the moon crossed the second star of Room.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Generals will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication points to grief for field commanders.

translations.literal: That seventh month Minister of Education Chen Jiao died.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month Minister of Education Chen Jiao died.

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year Minister of Education Han Ji died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year Minister of Education Han Ji died.

sentences.zh: 其七月辛卯，太白晝見，積二百八十餘日。

translations.literal: On xinmao in the seventh month the Great White was seen in daytime, lasting more than two hundred eighty days.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the seventh month Venus stayed up by daylight for more than two hundred eighty days.

sentences.zh: 時公孫文懿自立為燕王，署置百官，發兵距守，宣帝討滅之。

translations.literal: At that time Gongsun Wenyi had declared himself King of Yan, appointed a full bureaucracy, and mobilized for defense; Xuandi campaigned and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan had enthroned himself in Yan, set up an entire court, and armed the borders until Xuandi’s expedition annihilated him.

sentences.zh: 二年二月己丑，月犯心距星，又犯中央大星。

translations.literal: On jichou in the second month of the second year the Moon transgressed the separator stars of the Heart and also the great central star.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou in the second month the moon crossed both the Heart’s separator stars and its central luminary.

sentences.zh: 五月乙亥，月又犯心距星及中央大星。

translations.literal: On yihai in the fifth month the Moon again transgressed the separator stars and the great central star.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the fifth month the moon repeated those transits.

translations.literal: Investigating the omen-text it says: “The king finds it ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: The archived gloss states that the ruler should dread the sign.

translations.literal: Transgressing the front star means the heir apparent will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Striking the leading star of the Heart imperils the crown prince.

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died in the third year’s first month.

translations.literal: The heir apparent was enthroned but soon deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The new sovereign was enthroned yet promptly cast aside.

translations.literal: That tenth month, on wuwu, the Moon transgressed the Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the tenth month the moon crossed the Winnowing Basket.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Generals will die.
translations.idiomatic: The reading foretells a general’s death.

sentences.zh: 」正始元年四月，車騎將軍黃權薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first Zhengshi year General of Chariots and Cavalry Huang Quan died.
translations.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry Huang Quan died in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1.

sentences.zh: 其閏十一月癸丑，月犯心中央大星。

translations.literal: On guichou in the intercalary eleventh month the Moon transgressed the great central star of the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the intercalary eleventh month the moon crossed the Heart’s central star.

sentences.zh: 少帝正始元年四月戊午，月犯昴東頭第一星。

translations.literal: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 the Moon transgressed the first star at the eastern end of the Hairy Head [Pleiades region].
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 the moon clipped the easternmost star of the Hairy Head.

sentences.zh: 十月庚寅，月又犯昴北斗四星。

translations.literal: On gengyin in the tenth month the Moon again transgressed the Hairy Head and the four stars of the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin in the tenth month the moon transited both the Hairy Head and four stars of the Northern Dipper.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Moon transgresses the Hairy Head, the Hu are restless.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss warns that lunar trespass on the Hairy Head stirs the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 」二年六月，鮮卑阿妙兒等寇西方，敦煌太守王延破之，斬二萬餘級。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year Xianbei under Amiao’er and others raided the west; prefect Wang Yan of Dunhuang defeated them and beheaded more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year’s sixth month Xianbei bands led by Amiao’er struck the western marches; Dunhuang prefect Wang Yan routed them, claiming over twenty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 三年，又斬鮮卑大師及千餘級。

translations.literal: In the third year another campaign severed the Xianbei commander’s head and over a thousand others.
translations.idiomatic: The third year saw another victory that took the Xianbei commander’s head plus more than a thousand others.

sentences.zh: 二年九月癸酉，月犯輿鬼西北星。

translations.literal: On guiyou in the ninth month of the second year the Moon transgressed the northwest star of the Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the second year’s ninth month the moon crossed the Ghosts’ northwest star.

sentences.zh: 三年二月丁未，又犯西南星。

translations.literal: On dingwei in the third year’s second month it again transgressed the southwest star.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the third year’s second month it struck the Ghosts’ southwest star.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be an ordinance on coinage.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication speaks of an edict touching currency or minting.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Great ministers will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: A variant gloss adds: “High ministers face peril.”

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year Grand Commandant Man Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Man Chong died in the third month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，帝加元服，賜群臣錢各有差。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the emperor assumed the capping [adult rite] and bestowed cash on the various ministers in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth year’s first month saw the emperor’s capping ceremony and graded cash gifts to his officials.

sentences.zh: 四年十月、十一月，月再犯井鉞。

translations.literal: In the tenth and eleventh months of the fourth year the Moon twice transgressed the Well’s Battle-Axe.
translations.idiomatic: During the fourth year’s tenth and eleventh months the moon crossed the Well’s axe twice.

sentences.zh: 是月，宣帝討諸葛恪，恪棄城走。

translations.literal: That same month Xuandi campaigned against Zhuge Ke, who abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That month Xuandi attacked Zhuge Ke, who deserted his walls and ran.

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year Cao Shuang campaigned against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang led a Shu expedition in the fifth year’s second month.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月癸巳，填星犯亢距星。

translations.literal: On guisi in the eleventh month of the fifth year the Station Star transgressed the separator stars of the Neck [lodge].
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in the fifth year’s eleventh month Saturn crossed the Neck’s separator stars.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Among the feudal lords there will be one who loses his state.
translations.idiomatic: The reading warns that a regional lord will forfeit his realm.

translations.literal: On dingchou in the seventh month of the seventh year the Moon transgressed the left horn [of the Horn lodge].
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the seventh year’s seventh month the moon crossed the Horn’s left horn-star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天下有兵，左將軍死。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Under Heaven there will be soldiers; the general of the left will die.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss predicts widespread arms and the death of the commander of the left.

translations.literal: On yihai in the seventh month Spark-Delight transgressed the separator star of the Net.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the seventh month Mars crossed the Net’s separator star.

translations.literal: The omen-text says:
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication reads:

translations.literal: There will be troops on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Border garrisons will mobilize.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Punishments will be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Another line adds that penal sanctions will be enforced.

translations.literal: On xinhai in the first month of the ninth year the Moon transgressed the southern star of the Neck.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the ninth year’s first month the moon crossed the Neck’s southern star.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Arms will arise.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation foretells warfare.

translations.literal: Another saying: “A general will die.
translations.idiomatic: A variant warns of a general’s death.

translations.literal: On guichou in the seventh month the Station Star transgressed Key-and-Bolt.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the seventh month Saturn crossed Key-and-Bolt.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「王者不宜出宮下殿。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The king should not leave the palace or descend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss advises the ruler against traveling beyond the palace or stepping down from the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 」嘉平元年，天子謁陵，宣帝奏誅曹爽等。

translations.literal: In the first Jiaping year the Son of Heaven visited the imperial tombs; Xuandi memorialized to execute Cao Shuang and his party.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaping 1 saw the emperor tend the tombs while Xuandi procured orders to purge Cao Shuang’s faction.

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven lodged in the field encampment; thereby he lost authority.
translations.idiomatic: Forced to camp outside the capital, the emperor forfeited real power.

sentences.zh: 嘉平元年六月壬戌，太白犯東井距星。

translations.literal: On renxu in the sixth month of Jiaping 1 the Great White transgressed the separator stars of the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in Jiaping 1’s sixth month Venus crossed the Eastern Well’s separator stars.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The state loses good government; great ministers make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The reading describes misrule and ministerial revolt.

translations.literal: On xinsi in the fourth month the Great White transgressed the Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the fourth month Venus entered the Ghosts.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Great ministers will be executed.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss predicts executions among chief ministers.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Arms will arise.
translations.idiomatic: An alternate line again forecasts war.

sentences.zh: 」二年三月己未，太白又犯井距星。

translations.literal: On jiwei in the third month of the second year the Great White again transgressed the Well’s separator stars.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei in the second year’s third month Venus repeated its crossing of the Well’s separator stars.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，王淩與楚王彪有謀，皆伏誅，人主遂卑。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year Wang Ling conspired with Prince Biao of Chu; both were executed; the ruler’s prestige thereafter sank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year’s third month Wang Ling and Prince Biao of Chu were exposed and killed for plotting, humbling the throne.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權赤烏十三年夏五月，日北至，熒惑逆行，入南斗。

translations.literal: In Wu, Sun Quan’s thirteenth Chiwu year, summer, fifth month, the sun reached its northern limit and Spark-Delight moved retrograde into the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu’s Chiwu 13, fifth summer month, at the summer solstice Mars retrograded into the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，犯魁第三星而東。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, it transgressed the third star of the Dipper’s bowl and proceeded eastward.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, seventh month, it crossed the Dipper’s third “handle” star and continued east.

translations.literal: The “Han–Jin Spring and Autumn” states “retrograde motion.”
translations.idiomatic: The *Han–Jin Spring and Autumn* records the planet’s retrograde motion.

sentences.zh: 案占：「熒惑入南斗，三月吳王死。

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: “When Spark-Delight enters the Southern Dipper, within three months the king of Wu will die.
translations.idiomatic: Archive glosses say Mars in the Southern Dipper means the Wu sovereign dies within three months.

translations.literal: Another saying: “When Spark-Delight moves retrograde, the region beneath it will lose its ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss ties retrograde Mars to the death of whatever ruler lies below.

sentences.zh: 」太元二年，權薨，是其應也，故《國志》書于吳。

translations.literal: In the second Taiyuan year Sun Quan died—exactly the fulfillment—so the “National Records” records it under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan died in Taiyuan 2, matching the omen, which is why the Wu annals preserve the entry.

sentences.zh: 是時，王淩謀立楚王彪，謂「斗中有星，當有暴貴者」，以問知星人浩詳。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Ling plotted to enthrone Prince Biao of Chu, saying “There is a star in the Dipper—someone base will suddenly rise to honor,” and questioned the star-clerk Haoxiang about it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling, scheming to raise Prince Biao, cited an extraordinary star in the Dipper and consulted the astrologer Haoxiang.

sentences.zh: 詳疑有故，欲悅其意，不言吳有死喪，而言「淮南楚分，吳楚同占，當有王者興」，故淩計遂定。

translations.literal: Haoxiang suspected ulterior motives and, wishing to please him, avoided speaking of Wu’s mourning omen and instead said “Huainan belongs to Chu’s quarter; Wu and Chu share the same divination—there a new king will arise,” so Wang Ling’s plan hardened.
translations.idiomatic: Haoxiang sensed danger and flattered Wang Ling by omitting Wu’s death portent, claiming Huainan’s Chu sector meant a new king would rise, which sealed Ling’s resolve.

sentences.zh: 嘉平二年十二月丙申，月犯輿鬼。

translations.literal: On bingshen in the twelfth month of Jiaping 2 the Moon transgressed the Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in Jiaping 2’s twelfth month the moon crossed the Ghosts.

sentences.zh: 三年四月戊寅，月犯東井。

translations.literal: On wuyin in the fourth month of the third year the Moon transgressed the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the third year’s fourth month the moon entered the Eastern Well.

translations.literal: On jiayin in the fifth month the Moon transgressed the Neck’s separator stars.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the fifth month the moon crossed the Neck’s separator stars.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “A general will die.
translations.idiomatic: The reading forecasts a general’s death.

translations.literal: Another saying: “There will be soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: An alternate gloss predicts warfare.

translations.literal: That month Wang Ling, Prince Biao of Chu, and their accomplices were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wang Ling, Prince Biao, and associates were put to death.

translations.literal: In the seventh month Empress Zhen died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhen died in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，吳將為寇，鎮東將軍諸葛誕破走之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year Wu generals raided the borders; General Who Guards the East Zhuge Dan routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu raiders struck in the fourth year’s third month until Zhuge Dan, general who guards the east, drove them off.

sentences.zh: 其年七月己巳，月犯輿鬼。

translations.literal: That seventh month, on jisi, the Moon transgressed the Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi that seventh month the moon crossed the Ghosts again.

translations.literal: On yisi in the ninth month it transgressed them again.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the ninth month it repeated the transit.

sentences.zh: 十月癸未，熒惑犯亢南星。

translations.literal: On guiwei in the tenth month Spark-Delight transgressed the southern star of the Neck.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the tenth month Mars crossed the Neck’s southern star.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Ministers will revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss speaks of ministerial sedition.

sentences.zh: 」四年十一月丁未，月又犯鬼積尸。

translations.literal: On dingwei in the fourth year’s eleventh month the Moon again transgressed the heaped corpses in the Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the fourth year’s eleventh month the moon crossed the Ghosts’ ‘piled corpses’ stars.

sentences.zh: 五年六月戊午，太白犯角。

translations.literal: On wuwu in the fifth year’s sixth month the Great White transgressed the Horn.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the fifth year’s sixth month Venus crossed the Horn.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Ministers will plot but not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The reading describes plots among ministers that miscarry.

translations.literal: On gengchen the Moon transgressed the Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the moon crossed the Winnowing Basket.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “A general will die.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication predicts a general’s death.

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Moon transgressed the Well’s Battle-Axe.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month the moon crossed the Well’s axe.

translations.literal: On bingwu the Moon again transgressed the northwest star of the Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the moon repeated its strike on the Ghosts’ northwest star.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The state will have sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss warns of national mourning.

translations.literal: On guiyou in the eleventh month the Moon transgressed the separator stars of the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the eleventh month the moon crossed the Eastern Well’s separator stars.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “A general will die.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation again signals a general’s death.

sentences.zh: 」正元元年正月，鎮東將軍毋丘儉、揚州刺史文欽反，兵俱敗，誅死。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first Zhengyuan year General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian and Inspector of Yangzhou Wen Qin rebelled; both armies were crushed and the leaders executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyuan 1 opened with Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin’s rebellion—both forces were destroyed and the generals slain.

sentences.zh: 二月，李豐及弟翼、後父張緝等謀亂，事泄，悉誅，皇后張氏廢。

translations.literal: In the second month Li Feng, his younger brother Li Yi, his father-in-law Zhang Ji, and others plotted sedition; the affair leaked and all were executed; Empress Zhang was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The second month exposed Li Feng, Li Yi, Zhang Ji, and fellow conspirators, who were killed, and Empress Zhang was cast down.

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor was deposed as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth month reduced the emperor to Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 蜀將姜維攻隴西，車騎將軍郭淮討破之。

translations.literal: Shu general Jiang Wei attacked Longxi; General of Chariots and Cavalry Guo Huai defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei’s Longxi offensive failed against Guo Huai, general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公正元二年二月戊午，熒惑犯東井北轅西頭第一星。

translations.literal: On wuwu in the second month of the second Zhengyuan year of the Duke of Gaoguixiang Spark-Delight transgressed the first western star at the northern yoke of the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in Zhengyuan 2’s second month Mars crossed the westernmost star on the Well’s northern pole.

sentences.zh: 甘露元年七月乙卯，熒惑犯東井鉞星。

translations.literal: On yimao in the seventh month of Ganlu 1 Spark-Delight transgressed the battle-axe star of the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in Ganlu 1’s seventh month Mars crossed the Eastern Well’s axe star.

translations.literal: On renxu the Moon again transgressed the axe star.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the moon repeated the axe transit.

translations.literal: On xinhai in the eighth month the Moon transgressed the Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the eighth month the moon crossed the Winnowing Basket.

sentences.zh: 吳廢孫亮太平元年九月壬辰，太白犯南斗，《吳志》所書也。

translations.literal: Wu’s deposed emperor Sun Liang, Taiping first year, ninth month, renchen day—what the “Wu Treatise” records—is the Great White transgressing the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The *Wu Treatise* entry for Taiping 1, ninth month renchen under Sun Liang records Venus crossing the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「太白犯斗，國有兵，大臣有反者。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Great White transgresses the Dipper, the state has troops and great ministers rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss ties Venus in the Dipper to civil war and ministerial revolt.

translations.literal: The next year Zhuge Dan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan rose in rebellion the following year.

translations.literal: The year after that Sun Lin deposed Sun Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin removed Sun Liang the year after.

translations.literal: Wu and Wei alike saw campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Both Wu and Wei knew martial crises.

sentences.zh: 甘露元年九月丁巳，月犯東井。

translations.literal: On dingsi in the ninth month of Ganlu 1 the Moon transgressed the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in Ganlu 1’s ninth month the moon entered the Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 二年六月己酉，月犯心中央大星。

translations.literal: On jiyou in the sixth month of the second year the Moon transgressed the great central star of the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the second year’s sixth month the moon crossed the Heart’s central star.

translations.literal: On renzi in the eighth month the Year Star transgressed the Well’s Battle-Axe.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the eighth month Jupiter crossed the Well’s axe.

sentences.zh: 九月庚寅，歲星逆行，乘井鉞。

translations.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month the Year Star moved retrograde and rode atop the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter then retrograded onto the battle-axe stars.

sentences.zh: 十月丙寅，太白犯亢距星。

translations.literal: On bingyin in the tenth month the Great White transgressed the Neck’s separator stars.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the tenth month Venus crossed the Neck’s separator stars.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Rebellious ministers make turmoil; the ruler grieves.
translations.idiomatic: The reading describes traitorous ministers and the sovereign’s distress.

sentences.zh: 」景元元年五月，有成濟之變及諸葛誕誅，皆其應也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Jingyuan 1 the Chen Ji coup and Zhuge Dan’s execution fulfilled it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan 1’s fifth month brought the Chen Ji incident and Zhuge Dan’s destruction, matching the signs.

sentences.zh: 二年三月庚子，太白犯東井。

translations.literal: On gengzi in the third month of the second year the Great White transgressed the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi in the second year’s third month Venus entered the Eastern Well.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The state loses good government; great ministers make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss repeats warnings of misrule and ministerial revolt.

translations.literal: That night the Year Star again transgressed the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Jupiter repeated its entry into the Eastern Well.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Arms will arise.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication predicts warfare.

translations.literal: By Jingyuan 1 the Duke of Gaoguixiang had been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: By Jingyuan 1 the reign of the Duke of Gaoguixiang ended in ruin.

sentences.zh: 三年八月壬辰，歲星犯輿鬼鑕星。

translations.literal: On renchen in the eighth month of the third year the Year Star transgressed the sentencing stars of the Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the third year’s eighth month Jupiter crossed the Ghosts’ execution stars.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Axes of punishment are used; great ministers are executed.
translations.idiomatic: The reading describes capital punishment falling on high officials.

sentences.zh: 」四年四月甲申，歲星又犯輿鬼東南星。

translations.literal: On jiashen in the fourth year’s fourth month the Year Star again transgressed the southeastern star of the Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the fourth year’s fourth month Jupiter struck the Ghosts’ southeast star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「鬼東南星主兵，木入鬼，大臣誅。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The southeastern star of the Ghosts governs soldiers; when wood enters the Ghosts, great ministers are executed.
translations.idiomatic: Archivists explain that the Ghosts’ southeast star commands armies and Jupiter’s entry means ministers die.

translations.literal: In Jingyuan 1 Minister Secretary Wang Jing was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan 1 saw Minister Secretary Wang Jing executed.

sentences.zh: 元帝景元元年二月，月犯建星。

translations.literal: In the second month of Jingyuan 1 of Emperor Yuan of Jin the Moon transgressed the Establishment Stars.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan’s Jingyuan 1, second month, the moon crossed the Establishment asterism.

sentences.zh: 案占：「月五星犯建星，大臣相譖。

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: “When the Moon or the Five Planets transgress the Establishment Stars, great ministers slander one another.
translations.idiomatic: Library glosses say lunar or planetary strikes on the Establishment Stars mean ministers backbite each other.

translations.literal: Afterward Zhong Hui and Deng Ai conquered Shu, and Hui slandered Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui and Deng Ai then destroyed Shu, after which Hui framed Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，熒惑入太微，犯右執法。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year Spark-Delight entered the Supreme Palace and transgressed the Right Enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: The second year’s fourth month brought Mars into the Supreme Palace across the Right Enforcer.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The ruler has great sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation warns of grave grief for the sovereign.

translations.literal: One version: “Great ministers will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: One annotation stresses sorrow for great ministers instead.

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year the Year Star stationed at the Room [lodge].
translations.idiomatic: The fourth year’s tenth month saw Jupiter station in the Room.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Generals and ministers will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss speaks of grief for generals and ministers.

translations.literal: One version: “There will be a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Another version promises a sweeping pardon.

sentences.zh: 」明年，鄧艾、鍾會皆夷滅，赦蜀土。

translations.literal: The next year Deng Ai and Zhong Hui were exterminated to the last generation and Shu territory was amnestied.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Deng Ai and Zhong Hui’s lineages were wiped out while conquered Shu received clemency.

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor abdicated.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth year witnessed the emperor’s abdication.

sentences.zh: 武帝咸寧四年九月，太白當見不見。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth Xianning year of Emperor Wu the Great White ought to have appeared but did not.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu’s Xianning 4 ninth month should have shown Venus at dawn yet the planet stayed hidden.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「是謂失舍，不有破軍，必有亡國。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “This is called ‘missing its lodging’; if not the destruction of an army, then surely the loss of a state.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss calls it ‘abandoning its station’: expect either a shattered army or a fallen dynasty.

translations.literal: At that time Yang Hu submitted a memorial requesting to attack Wu, and the sovereign approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu tabled a plan to invade Wu and the throne gave its assent.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月，兵出，太白始夕見西方。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year troops marched out, and the Great White first appeared in the west at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: That November the armies advanced while Venus made its first evening appearance in the west.

sentences.zh: 太康元年三月，大破吳軍，孫皓面縛請罪，吳國遂亡。

translations.literal: In the third month of Taikang 1 Wu’s armies were utterly defeated; Sun Hao bound himself and pleaded guilt, and the state of Wu perished.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 1’s third month shattered Wu’s forces; Sun Hao came bound in surrender and Wu collapsed.

sentences.zh: 太康八年三月，熒惑守心。

translations.literal: In the third month of Taikang 8 Spark-Delight stationed at the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 8’s third month saw Mars lodge upon Antares.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The king finds it ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication warns the sovereign.

translations.literal: On yiyou in the fourth month of Tixi 1 the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died on yiyou in Tixi 1’s fourth month.

sentences.zh: 惠帝元康三年四月，熒惑守太微六十日。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Yuan-kang 3 of Emperor Hui Spark-Delight stationed in the Supreme Palace for sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui’s Yuan-kang 3 fourth month held Mars sixty days inside the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「諸侯三公謀其上，必有斬臣。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Marquises and the Three Dukes plot against their ruler; there must be executed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss speaks of nobles and chief ministers conspiring against the throne and paying with their lives.

translations.literal: Another saying: “The Son of Heaven loses his state.
translations.idiomatic: A variant predicts outright loss of the dynasty.

translations.literal: That spring the Great White stationed at the Net, and by then it had remained more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: The same spring Venus lodged in the Net for over a hundred days.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be fear of sudden edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The reading warns of hasty proclamations and alarm.

translations.literal: Another saying: “The minister will die.
translations.idiomatic: Another line targets the chief minister’s death.

translations.literal: It also means uneasy frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: It further signals disturbed borders.

translations.literal: Afterward Empress Jia framed and murdered the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia later destroyed the crown prince by false accusation.

sentences.zh: 六年十月乙未，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On yiwei in the sixth month of the ninth year the Great White was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the ninth year’s sixth month Venus appeared by daylight.

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year Spark-Delight stationed at the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth year’s sixth month again placed Mars on the Heart.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The king finds it ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler should dread the sign.

translations.literal: In the eighth month Spark-Delight entered the Forbidden Guards asterism.
translations.idiomatic: That August Mars entered the imperial guard stars.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Palace troops will rise in force.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation predicts mobilization of the inner-army garrison.

sentences.zh: 」其後，帝見廢為太上皇，俄而三王起兵討趙王倫，倫悉遣中軍兵相距累月。

translations.literal: Thereafter the emperor was deposed as Retired Emperor; presently the Three Princes raised troops against Prince Zhao Lun, who dispatched the central army to oppose them for months on end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was soon reduced to Retired Emperor; then the three princes rose against Sima Lun, who threw the central corps against them for months.

sentences.zh: 永康元年三月，中台星坼，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the third month of Yongkang 1 the central terrace stars split, and the Great White appeared by day.
translations.idiomatic: Yongkang 1’s third month saw the asterism of the high ministers fracture while Venus shone in daylight.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When terrace stars lose their norm, the Three Dukes grieve.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss ties disorder among ministerial stars to danger for the Three Dukes.

translations.literal: The Great White seen by daylight means disloyal subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Daylight Venus signals rebellious ministers.

sentences.zh: 」是月，賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺後，斬司空張華。

translations.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir apparent; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and murdered the empress and beheaded Minister of Works Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: That month Empress Jia slew the heir; Sima Lun rapidly ousted and killed her and executed Zhang Hua.

translations.literal: That fifth month Spark-Delight entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth month brought Mars into the Southern Dipper.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The chief minister will die; troops rise on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: The reading promises a chief minister’s death and massive warfare.

translations.literal: The Dipper also marks Wu’s celestial field.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper likewise governs Wu’s astrological territory.

sentences.zh: 」是時，趙王倫為相，明年，篡位，三王興師誅之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Zhao Lun was chancellor; the next year he usurped the throne, and princes raised armies and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun held the premiership, seized the throne the following year, then fell to princely coalitions.

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai’an Shi Bing captured Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tai’an 2 saw Shi Bing overrun Yangzhou.

translations.literal: That eighth month Spark-Delight entered the Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: That August Mars entered the Winnowing Basket.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The ruler loses his throne; troops arise.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss forecasts loss of the throne and rebellion.

translations.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Sima Lun seized the throne and altered the reign title.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，太白出西方，逆行入東井。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year the Great White emerged in the west and moved retrograde into the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: The second year’s second month brought Venus out in the west, retrograding into the Eastern Well.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The state loses good government; great ministers make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation repeats warnings of misrule and ministerial revolt.

sentences.zh: 」是時，齊王冏起兵討趙王倫，倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奢，明年，誅死。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Qi Jiong raised troops against Prince Zhao Lun; Lun was destroyed, but Jiong kept his army from court, monopolized power, and indulged in arrogance and luxury; the next year he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi’s coalition destroyed Lun, yet Jiong quartered troops outside the capital, ruled tyrannically, and was killed the next year.

sentences.zh: 永甯元年，自正月至於閏月，五星互經天，縱橫無常。

translations.literal: In Yongning 1, from the first month through the intercalary month, all five planets crossed the sky by day, moving irregularly in every direction.
translations.idiomatic: From New Year through the leap month of Yongning 1 every planet transited the zenith by day, zigzagging without pattern.

translations.literal: The “Star Canon” says: “The sun is yang—the way of the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: The *Star Canon* teaches that the sun embodies yang and the sovereign’s path;

translations.literal: stars are yin—the way of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: stars embody yin and the ministers’ path.

sentences.zh: 日出則星亡，臣不得專也。

translations.literal: When the sun rises the stars vanish; ministers may not monopolize power.
translations.idiomatic: Sunrise extinguishes the stars, just as subjects must not seize authority.

sentences.zh: 晝而星見午上者為經天，其占為不臣，為更王。

translations.literal: Stars seen at noon upon crossing the sky count as ‘crossing heaven’; their interpretation is disloyal subjects and change of king.
translations.idiomatic: Planets crossing the meridian at noon are ‘sky-spanning,’ auguring rebellion and dynastic turnover.

sentences.zh: 」今五星悉經天，天變所未有也。

translations.literal: Now all five planets crossed the sky—a celestial anomaly never recorded before.
translations.idiomatic: Never had all five planets simultaneously transited the daytime sky.

sentences.zh: 石氏說曰：「辰星晝見，其國不亡則大亂。

translations.literal: Shi’s explanation says: “When the Dawn Star appears by day, if the state does not perish it suffers great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shen’s school adds that daytime Mercury means ruin or utter turmoil.

sentences.zh: 」是後，台鼎方伯，互執大權，二帝流亡，遂至六夷更王，迭據華夏，亦載籍所未有也。

translations.literal: Afterward ministers and regional shepherds seized power in turn; two emperors went into exile; eventually six barbarian peoples enthroned rulers in succession and carved up the Central Plains—another spectacle absent from the annals.
translations.idiomatic: Later Three Dukes and provincial governors wrested authority; two sovereigns fled; six successive alien regimes partitioned China—again without precedent in the records.

translations.literal: That fourth month the Year Star appeared by day.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth month showed Jupiter in daylight.

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Great White appeared by day.
translations.idiomatic: May brought Venus out at noon.

translations.literal: The interpretation matches the foregoing.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss matched earlier entries.

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Year Star stationed at Emptiness and Rooftop.
translations.idiomatic: July stationed Jupiter over Emptiness and Rooftop.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When wood stations at Emptiness and Rooftop there is military sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The reading ties Jupiter there to martial calamity.

translations.literal: Emptiness and Rooftop mark Qi’s field.
translations.idiomatic: Those lodges correspond to the Qi region.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Stationing at Emptiness means famine;
translations.idiomatic: One gloss adds famine for Emptiness;

translations.literal: stationing at Rooftop means corvée labor grows vexing and the common people are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: stationing at Rooftop means grinding labor service and a drained populace.

sentences.zh: 」辰星入太微，占曰「為內亂」，一曰「群臣相殺」。

translations.literal: The Dawn Star entered the Supreme Palace; the interpretation reads ‘internal rebellion,’ another variant reads ‘ministers slaughter one another.’
translations.idiomatic: Mercury’s entry into the Supreme Palace glosses as palace turmoil or ministers killing each other.

sentences.zh: 太白守右掖門，占曰：「為兵，為亂，為賊。

translations.literal: The Great White guarded the right-side gate of the Forbidden Palace; the interpretation reads ‘soldiers, turmoil, banditry.’
translations.idiomatic: Venus lodged on the Supreme Palace’s right gate, auguring arms, chaos, and brigandage.

sentences.zh: 」八月戊午，填星犯左執法，又犯上相，占曰「上相憂」。

translations.literal: On wuwu in the eighth month the Station Star transgressed the Left Enforcer and again the Upper Minister; the interpretation reads ‘the upper minister grieves.’
translations.idiomatic: August wuwu saw Saturn strike the Left Enforcer and Upper Minister with omens for the senior minister.

sentences.zh: 熒惑守昴，占曰「趙魏有災」。

translations.literal: Spark-Delight stationed at the Hairy Head; the interpretation reads ‘calamity for Zhao and Wei.’
translations.idiomatic: Mars lingering on the Hairy Head threatened Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 辰星守輿鬼，占曰「秦有災」。

translations.literal: The Dawn Star guarded the Ghosts; the interpretation reads ‘calamity for Qin.’
translations.idiomatic: Mercury lodging on the Ghosts foretold disaster for Qin.

translations.literal: On dingwei in the ninth month the Moon transgressed the left horn.
translations.idiomatic: September dingwei brought a lunar transit of the Horn’s left spike.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The ruler will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign should grieve.

translations.literal: Another saying: “The commander of the Left Guards dies; under Heaven there will be troops.
translations.idiomatic: Another clause predicts the Left Guards general’s death and empire-wide arms.

translations.literal: On guiyou in the fourth month of the second year the Year Star appeared by day.
translations.idiomatic: Second year fourth month guiyou showed Jupiter by daylight.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Ministers grow powerful.
translations.idiomatic: The reading warns of overpowerful ministers.

sentences.zh: 」初，齊王冏定京都，因留輔政，遂專慠無君。

translations.literal: Earlier Prince Qi had pacified the capital and stayed to assist government, then turned arrogant and lordly beyond his king.
translations.idiomatic: After securing Luoyang Prince Qi remained as regent and slid into heedless arrogance.

sentences.zh: 是月，成都、河間檄長沙王乂討之，冏乂交戰，攻焚宮闕，冏兵敗，夷滅。

translations.literal: That month Chengdu and Hejian issued summons for Prince Changsha Yi to campaign against him; armies of Yi and Jiong clashed, palace gates burned, Jiong’s troops were ruined and exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu and Hejian called on Prince Changsha to attack Qi; their forces fought through the palace, torched the halls, and annihilated Jiong.

sentences.zh: 又殺其兄上軍將軍寔以下二十餘人。

translations.literal: They also executed General of the Upper Army Shi—Jiong’s elder brother—along with more than twenty others.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty were put to death with Jiong’s elder brother, General of the Upper Army Shi.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，成都攻長沙，於是公私饑困，百姓力屈。

translations.literal: In Tai’an 2 Chengdu attacked Changsha; public and private stores alike failed until the people had nothing left to give.
translations.idiomatic: Tai’an 2’s Chengdu–Changsha war emptied granaries and broke the commoners.

sentences.zh: 太安二年二月，太白入昴。

translations.literal: In the second month of Tai’an 2 the Great White entered the Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: Tai’an 2’s second month saw Venus enter the Hairy Head.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Under Heaven is disturbed; troops rise on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: The realm convulses with widespread warfare.

translations.literal: In the seventh month Spark-Delight entered the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: July brought Mars into the Eastern Well.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Arms arise; the state is in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss predicts rebellion and national chaos.

translations.literal: That autumn the Great White guarded the Supreme Palace’s Upper First Minister.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Venus stationed on the Upper First Minister star.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The upper first minister perishes by arms.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation says the premier falls to weapons.

translations.literal: That winter Chengdu and Hejian attacked Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Winter saw Chengdu and Hejian strike the capital.

sentences.zh: 八月，長沙王奉帝出距二王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Prince Changsha led the emperor forth to resist the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changsha escorted the emperor out to face the allied armies.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，東海王越執長沙王乂，張方又殺之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Prince Donghai Yue seized Prince Changsha Yi, and Zhang Fang murdered him.
translations.idiomatic: Third year’s first month Sima Yue arrested Prince Changsha; Zhang Fang killed him.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，熒惑入南斗，占同永康。

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month Spark-Delight entered the Southern Dipper; the interpretation matches the Yongkang case.
translations.idiomatic: Third year’s first month Mars entered the Dipper with the same gloss recorded under Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 七月，左衛將軍陳眕率眾奉帝伐成都，六軍敗績，兵逼乘輿。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Commander of the Left Guards Chen Zhen led troops escorting the emperor to campaign against Chengdu; the six armies were routed and soldiers pressed the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: July saw Chen Zhen march the emperor west against Chengdu; the imperial hosts collapsed and threatened the sovereign’s train.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下盜賊群起，張昌尤盛。

translations.literal: At that time bandits sprang up everywhere; Zhang Chang was fiercest.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels erupted empire-wide, Zhang Chang foremost.

sentences.zh: 永興元年七月庚申，太白犯角、亢，經房、心，歷尾、箕。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the seventh month of Yongxing 1 the Great White transgressed the Horn and Neck, passed through Room and Heart, and crossed Tail and Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing 1’s seventh month gengshen placed Venus across Horn through Tail.

translations.literal: In the ninth month it entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: September brought it into the Southern Dipper.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Transgressing the Horn means great war under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Striking the Horn forecasts empire-wide battle;

translations.literal: transgressing the Neck means great armies and the ruler’s sorrow;
translations.idiomatic: striking the Neck means massive hosts and the emperor’s grief;

translations.literal: entering Room and Heart means armies and mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Room and Heart augur campaigns and funerals;

translations.literal: transgressing Tail and Winnowing Basket means the principal consort will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Tail and Winnowing Basket threaten the empress.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Under Heaven falls into great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss predicts utter turmoil.

translations.literal: Entering the Southern Dipper means armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Entry into the Dipper couples arms with bereavement.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Generals will rebel.
translations.idiomatic: A variant warns of mutinous commanders.

sentences.zh: 其所犯守，又兗、豫、幽、冀、揚州之分野。

translations.literal: The lodges it invaded and guarded correspond to Yan, Yu, You, Ji, and Yang provinces’ fields.
translations.idiomatic: Those celestial precincts map onto Yan, Yu, You, Ji, and Yang.

translations.literal: That seventh month saw the battle at Dangyin.
translations.idiomatic: July brought the Dangyin slaughter.

sentences.zh: 九月，王浚殺幽州刺史和演，攻鄴，鄴潰，於是兗豫為天下兵衝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wang Jun killed Inspector of Youzhou He Yan, attacked Ye, Ye fell, and Yanzhou and Yuzhou became the empire’s military choke points.
translations.idiomatic: September Wang Jun slew He Yan, stormed Ye, and turned Yan-Yu into battle highways.

translations.literal: Chen Min then rebelled across the Yangzhou lands.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min next seized the southeast.

sentences.zh: 劉元海、石勒、李雄等並起微賤，跨有州郡。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan, Shi Le, Li Xiong, and others alike rose from humble stations and straddled whole provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan, Shi Le, Li Xiong, and peers climbed from obscurity to hold regional sway.

translations.literal: Empress Yang was repeatedly imprisoned and deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang suffered repeated deposition and house arrest.

translations.literal: All were its fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Each event answered the omens.

sentences.zh: 二年四月丙子，太白犯狼星。

translations.literal: On bingzi in the fourth month of the second year the Great White transgressed the Wolf Star.
translations.idiomatic: Second year fourth month bingzi saw Venus cross the Wolf.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Great armies arise.
translations.idiomatic: Massive campaigns follow.

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Year Star guarded the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: September stationed Jupiter on the Eastern Well.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be troops; the Well moreover marks Qin’s field.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss predicts warfare, and the Well belongs to Qin’s asterism.

sentences.zh: 」是年，苟晞破公師籓，張方破范陽王猇，關西諸將攻河間王顒，顒奔走，東海王迎殺之。

translations.literal: That year Gou Xi defeated Gongshi Fan, Zhang Fang crushed Prince Fanyang Xiao, western passes besieged Prince Hejian Yong—Yong fled, and Prince Donghai welcomed and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gou Xi broke Gongshi Fan, Zhang Fang routed Prince Fanyang, western columns trapped Prince Hejian until he fled and Sima Yue killed him.

sentences.zh: 光熙元年四月，太白失行，自翼入尾、箕。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Guangxi 1 the Great White lost proper motion, moving from Wings into Tail and Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi 1’s fourth month showed Venus erratic, sliding from Wings down to Tail.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「太白失行而北，是謂反生。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Great White loses proper motion and heads north, this is called ‘reversed birth.’
translations.idiomatic: The gloss labels northward erratic Venus as ‘reverse birth,’ an uncanny motion.

translations.literal: If not the destruction of an army, then surely the slaughter of a city.
translations.idiomatic: Expect either an army’s ruin or a city put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 」五月，汲桑攻鄴，魏郡太守馮嵩出戰，大敗，桑遂害東燕王騰，殺萬餘人，焚燒魏時宮室皆盡。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Ji Sang attacked Ye; Administrator Feng Song of Wei Commandery gave battle and was utterly defeated; Sang then slew Prince Teng of Eastern Yan, killed more than ten thousand persons, and burned every Wei-era palace structure to ash.
translations.idiomatic: May brought Ji Sang’s assault on Ye—Feng Song met disaster, Sima Teng died, ten thousand fell, and Wei’s old palaces burned bare.

translations.literal: That ninth month on dingwei Spark-Delight stationed at the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the ninth month Mars lodged on Antares.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The king finds it ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign should dread it.

translations.literal: On jihai the Station Star guarded Room and Heart.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Saturn stationed across Room and Heart.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Station guards Room, many calamities and funeral rites;
translations.idiomatic: Saturn lingering on Room brings repeated mourning;

translations.literal: when it guards Heart, there is turmoil inside the state and an empire-wide amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: on Heart it promises civil strife ended by general pardon.

sentences.zh: 」是時，司馬越專權，終以無禮破滅，內亂之應也。

translations.literal: At that time Sima Yue monopolized authority and finally perished through insolence—the response of internal rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue’s tyranny ended in destruction, matching the inner turmoil reading.

sentences.zh: 十一月，帝崩，懷帝即位，大赦天下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the emperor died; Emperor Huai succeeded and proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: November brought the emperor’s death; Emperor Huai mounted the throne with a universal amnesty.

sentences.zh: 懷帝永嘉元年十二月丁亥，星流震散。

translations.literal: On dinghai in the twelfth month of Yongjia 1 stars streamed like thunder peals scattering.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia 1’s twelfth month dinghai saw meteors streak as if lightning shattered.

sentences.zh: 按劉向說，天官列宿，在位之象；

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang’s explanation, celestial officers and arrayed lodges image those holding court;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang teaches that stellar officers mirror titled ministers;

sentences.zh: 其眾小星無名者，眾庶之類。

translations.literal: their multitude of small unnamed stars represent the common folk.
translations.idiomatic: countless faint stars stand for commoners.

sentences.zh: 此百官眾庶將流散之象也。

translations.literal: This is the image of officials and commoners about to scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sky foretells bureaucrats and masses fleeing.

sentences.zh: 是後天下大亂，百官萬姓，流移轉死矣。

translations.literal: Afterward under Heaven fell into great chaos; officials and myriad households drifted, shifted, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide collapse followed—nobles and peasants alike were uprooted and slain.

sentences.zh: 二年正月庚午，太白伏不見，二月庚子，始晨見東方，是謂當見不見，占同上條。

translations.literal: On gengwu in the first month the Great White hid and did not appear; on gengzi in the second month it first appeared at dawn in the east—this is called ‘ought to appear yet absent’; the interpretation matches the preceding article.
translations.idiomatic: January gengwu Venus vanished until February gengzi dawn brought its eastern return—the ‘failed apparition’ omen cited earlier.

sentences.zh: 其後破軍殺將，不可勝數，帝崩虜庭，中夏淪覆。

translations.literal: Afterward armies were shattered and generals killed beyond reckoning; the emperor died in captivity and the Central Plains collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Armies fell endlessly; the sovereign perished among barbarians and north China sank.

sentences.zh: 三年正月庚子，熒惑犯紫微。

translations.literal: On gengzi in the first month of the third year Spark-Delight transgressed Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Third year New Year’s gengzi placed Mars across the Purple Palace.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「當有野死之王，又為火燒宮。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be a king dead in the wilds, and moreover palace fires.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss predicts sovereigns dying abroad and halls consumed by flame.

sentences.zh: 」是時太史令高堂沖奏，乘輿宜遷幸，不然必無洛陽。

translations.literal: At that time Astrologer Royal Gao Tang Chong memorialized that the imperial carriage ought to move lest Luoyang be lost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Court astronomer Gao Tang Chong urged removing the court or losing Luoyang forever.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，劉曜、王彌入京都，焚燒宮廊，執帝歸平陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year Liu Yao and Wang Mi entered the capital district, burned palace corridors, seized the emperor, and returned him to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia 5’s sixth month saw Liu Yao and Wang Mi sack Luoyang, torch the halls, and drag the emperor to Pingyang.

translations.literal: In the third year the Station Star long guarded the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Year three kept Saturn moored in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「填星所居久者，其國有福。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Wherever the Station Star lingers long, that region gains blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Long Saturn residence traditionally blesses the matching territory.

sentences.zh: 」是時，安東將軍、琅邪王始有揚土。

translations.literal: At that time General Who Maintains the East, Prince of Langye, first held Yangzhou soil.
translations.idiomatic: Then Sima Rui of Langye secured the southeast.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，地動，陳卓以為是地動應也。

translations.literal: That eleventh month there was an earthquake; Chen Zhuo deemed it the seismic echo of that sign.
translations.idiomatic: November’s tremor—Chen Zhuo read it as heaven’s aftershock.

translations.literal: In the fifth year’s tenth month Spark-Delight stationed at the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: October of the fifth year lodged Mars on Antares.

sentences.zh: 六年六月丁卯，太白犯太微。

translations.literal: On dingmao in the sixth month of the sixth year the Great White transgressed the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year sixth month dingmao brought Venus through the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「兵入天子庭，王者惡之。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Soldiers enter the Son of Heaven’s courtyard; the king finds it ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss warns of troops inside the throne enclosure.

sentences.zh: 」七月，帝崩於寇庭，天下行服大臨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the emperor died among bandits; the realm donned mourning and held grand lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: July brought the emperor’s death in captivity and empire-wide mourning.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興元年七月，太白犯南斗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Taixing 1 of Emperor Yuan the Great White transgressed the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan’s Taixing 1 seventh month saw Venus cross the Dipper.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Wu and Yue will have troops; great men will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The reading assigns warfare to Wu-Yue and grief to magnates.

translations.literal: On jiashen in the second month of the second year Spark-Delight transgressed the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: Second year second month jiashen placed Mars in the Eastern Well.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Arms arise; noble ministers slaughter one another.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss predicts war and mutual killing among peers.

translations.literal: On jimao in the eighth month the Great White transgressed the great star of the Chariot Shaft.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month jimao saw Venus cross Regulus.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The rear palace will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: The harem faces peril.

sentences.zh: 」三年五月己戊子，太白入太微，又犯上將星。

translations.literal: On wuzi in the fifth month of the third year the Great White entered the Supreme Palace and again transgressed the Upper First Minister star.
translations.idiomatic: Third year fifth month wuzi sent Venus into the Supreme Palace across the Upper First Minister.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The Son of Heaven commands in person; the upper minister is executed.
translations.idiomatic: It speaks of an emperor leading armies while his premier dies.

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Great White transgressed the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: September repeated Venus’ Dipper crossing.

sentences.zh: 十月己亥，熒惑在東井，居五諸侯南，踟躕留積三十日。

translations.literal: In the tenth month on jihai Spark-Delight stood in the Eastern Well south of the Five Feudatories, hesitating and lingering thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: October jihai found Mars in the Well south of the Five Feudatories, tarrying a full month.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「熒惑守井二十日以上，大人憂。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When Spark-Delight guards the Well twenty days or more, great men suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Mars lingering on the Well beyond twenty days harms magnates.

translations.literal: Guarding the Five Feudatories means feudatories will suffer executions.
translations.idiomatic: Lodging on the Five Feudatories points to punished regional lords.

sentences.zh: 」永昌元年三月，王敦率江荊之眾來攻京都，六軍距戰，敗績，人主謝過而已。

translations.literal: In the third month of Yongchang 1 Wang Dun led Yang and Jiang armies against the capital; the six armies resisted but were routed, and the sovereign could only apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang 1’s third month Wang Dun struck Jiankang with river armies; imperial troops collapsed leaving only contrition.

sentences.zh: 於是殺護軍將軍周顗、尚書令刁協、驃騎將軍戴若思。

translations.literal: They then killed Protector-General Zhou Yi, Minister Secretary Diao Xie, and General of Agile Cavalry Dai Ruosi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi, Diao Xie, and Dai Ruosi died in the purge.

translations.literal: Moreover General Who Guards the North Liu Wei fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei escaped north.

sentences.zh: 四月，又殺湘州刺史譙王司馬承、鎮南將軍甘卓。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they also killed Inspector of Xiangzhou Prince Sima Cheng of Qiao and General Who Guards the South Gan Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: April added Prince Cheng of Qiao and Gan Zhuo to the slaughter.

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The intercalary December ended with the emperor’s death.

sentences.zh: 明帝太寧三年正月，熒惑逆行，入太微。
