translations.literal: In the third month’s first year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Third year New Year emperor died.

sentences.zh: 少帝正始元年十月乙酉，彗星見西方，在尾，長三丈，拂牽牛，犯太白。

translations.literal: On yiyou in the tenth month of Zhengshi 1 of Shaodi a comet appeared in the west at Tail three zhang long, brushing the Herdsman and transgressing the Great White.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhengshi comet in Tail.

translations.literal: On jiazi in the eleventh month it advanced to strike the Forbidden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: November comet entered Forbidden Guards.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「尾為燕，又為吳，牛亦吳越之分。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Tail is Yan and also Wu; Ox likewise marks Wu-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Tail and Ox tie to northeast and Wu.

sentences.zh: 太白為上將，羽林中軍兵。

translations.literal: The Great White is the upper general; Forbidden Guards are central troops.
translations.idiomatic: Venus equals marshal; guards equal palace army.

translations.literal: Wu-Yue will mourn while central armies stir.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast grieves—capital hosts march.

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year Wu dispatched three generals to raid the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Year two May Wu raided borders.

translations.literal: Crown Prince Deng of Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: Wu heir Deng died.

sentences.zh: 六月，宣帝討諸葛恪於皖。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Xuandi campaigned against Zhuge Ke at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: June Sima Yi attacked Zhuge Ke.

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Man Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong, Grand Commandant, passed away.

sentences.zh: 六年八月戊午，彗星見七星，長二尺，色白，進至張，積二十三日滅。

translations.literal: On wuwu in the sixth year’s eighth month a comet appeared in the Seven Stars two feet long, white, advancing to Zhang, vanishing after twenty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 6 August comet in Seven Stars.

sentences.zh: 七年十一月癸亥，又見軫，長一尺，積百五十六日滅。

translations.literal: On guihai in the eleventh month of the seventh year it again appeared in the Chariot one foot long, lasting 156 days.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year November comet in Chariot.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，又見昴，長六尺，色青白，芒西南指。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year it again appeared in the Hairy Head six feet long, bluish white, tail pointing southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year third month comet in Mao.

sentences.zh: 七月，又見翼，長二尺，進至軫，積四十二日滅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month it again appeared in Wings two feet long, reaching the Chariot, disappearing after forty-two days.
translations.idiomatic: July comet Wings to Chariot.

sentences.zh: 案占曰：「七星張為周分野，翼軫為楚，昴為趙魏。

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Seven Stars and Zhang are Zhou’s field; Wings and Chariot are Chu; Mao is Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Archives map stars to Zhou, Chu, Zhao-Wei.

sentences.zh: 彗所以除舊布新，主兵喪也。

translations.literal: Comets purge old and spread new; they preside over armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Comets mean renewal through war and grief.

sentences.zh: 」嘉平元年，宣帝誅曹爽兄弟及其党與，皆夷三族，京師嚴兵。

translations.literal: In Jiaping 1 Xuandi executed Cao Shuang’s brothers and faction to the third kin, tightening arms at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaping 1 Sima Yi purged Cao Shuang.

sentences.zh: 三年，誅楚王彪，又襲王淩於淮南。

translations.literal: In the third year he executed Prince Chu Biao and struck Wang Ling in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Year three killed Cao Biao and crushed Wang Ling.

translations.literal: Huainan is eastern Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan matches Chu.

translations.literal: Wei princes were confined at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei imperial kin were caged at Ye.

sentences.zh: 嘉平三年十一月癸亥，有星孛于營室，西行，積九十日滅。

translations.literal: On guihai in the third year of Jiaping a broom star appeared in Encampment moving west, fading after ninety days.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaping 3 November comet in Encampment.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning.

translations.literal: Encampment governs the rear palace—the inner chambers will soon riot.
translations.idiomatic: Encampment threatens harem strife.

sentences.zh: 」四年二月丁酉，彗星見西方，在胃，長五六丈，色白，芒南指，貫參，積二十日滅。

translations.literal: On dingyou in the fourth year’s second month a comet appeared in the west in Stomach five or six zhang long, white tail south, piercing Triaster, gone in twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year February western comet.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月，彗星又見軫，長五丈，在太微左執法西，東南指，積百九十日滅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year’s eleventh month a comet again appeared in the Chariot five zhang west of the Supreme Palace Left Enforcer, pointing southeast, lasting 190 days.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year November long comet by Supreme Palace.

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Stomach is Yanzhou’s field.
translations.idiomatic: Stomach equals Yanzhou.

translations.literal: Triaster governs arms.
translations.idiomatic: Triaster commands warfare.

translations.literal: The Supreme Palace is the Son of Heaven’s courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Palace is the imperial court.

translations.literal: Enforcers represent those holding government.
translations.idiomatic: Enforcer stars are ministers.

sentences.zh: 孛彗為兵喪，除舊布新之象。

translations.literal: Broom stars mean armies and mourning—purging old for new.
translations.idiomatic: Comets augur martial mourning.

sentences.zh: 」正元元年二月，李豐、豐弟翼、後父張緝等謀亂，皆誅，皇后亦廢。

translations.literal: In the second month of Zhengyuan 1 Li Feng, his brother Yi, father-in-law Zhang Ji, and others plotted sedition; all were executed and the empress deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyuan 1 Li Feng conspiracy died.

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor was deposed as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor demoted to Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公正元元年十一月，白氣出南斗側，廣數丈，長竟天。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Zhengyuan 1 of the Duke of Gaoguixiang white vapor issued beside the Southern Dipper several zhang wide stretching the whole sky.
translations.idiomatic: White aura by Dipper.

sentences.zh: 王肅曰：「蚩尤之旗也，東南其有亂乎！

translations.literal: Wang Su said: “This is Chiyou’s banner—will the southeast riot?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su called it Chiyou’s standard.

sentences.zh: 」二年正月，有彗星見於吳楚分，西北竟天。

translations.literal: In the second year’s first month a comet appeared in Wu-Chu field spanning the northwest sky.
translations.idiomatic: Year two comet over Wu-Chu.

sentences.zh: 鎮東大將軍毋丘儉等據淮南叛，景帝討平之。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian rebelled in Huainan until Emperor Jing suppressed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian’s Huainan revolt fell.

sentences.zh: 案占：「蚩尤旗見，王者征伐四方。

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “When Chiyou’s banner appears the king campaigns everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Chiyou banner means universal war.

translations.literal: Afterward he again campaigned Huainan and pacified Ba-Shu westward.
translations.idiomatic: Further Huainan and Shu expeditions.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吳主孫亮五鳳元年也。

translations.literal: That year was Sun Liang’s Wu calendar fifth Phoenix year.
translations.idiomatic: It matched Wu’s fifth Phoenix year.

translations.literal: Ox and Dipper mark Wu-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper-Ox govern Wu-Yue.

sentences.zh: 案占：「吳有兵喪，除舊布新之象也。

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Wu will suffer armies and mourning—purging the old.
translations.idiomatic: Wu faces cometary disaster.

sentences.zh: 」太平三年，孫綝盛兵圍宮，廢亮為會稽王，故《國志》又書于吳也。

translations.literal: In Taiping 3 Sun Lin surrounded the palace with hosts, deposing Liang as Prince of Kuaiji—so Wu annals record it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin deposed Sun Liang.

sentences.zh: 淮南江東同揚州地，故于時變見吳、楚。

translations.literal: Huainan and Jiangdong share Yangzhou ground—omens showed in Wu and Chu alike.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan and Wu share Yangzhou omens.

sentences.zh: 楚之分則魏之淮南，多與吳同災。

translations.literal: Chu’s partition includes Wei’s Huainan, sharing Wu’s calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan echoed Wu.

sentences.zh: 是以毋丘儉以孛為己應，遂起兵而敗。

translations.literal: Hence Guanqiu Jian took the comet as his own sign, rose, and was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Jian misread the comet and lost.

sentences.zh: 後三年，即魏甘露二年，諸葛誕又反淮南，吳遣將救之。

translations.literal: Three years later in Wei’s Ganlu 2 Zhuge Dan rebelled again in Wu while Wu sent rescuers.
translations.idiomatic: Ganlu 2 Zhuge Dan revolted.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，誕眾與吳兵死沒各數萬人，猶前長星之應也。

translations.literal: When the city fell tens of thousands of Dan’s men and Wu troops perished—matching the earlier long comet.
translations.idiomatic: Siege deaths fulfilled the comet.

sentences.zh: 甘露二年十一月，彗星見角，色白。

translations.literal: In Ganlu 2 eleventh month a comet appeared in Horn, white.
translations.idiomatic: Ganlu 2 November comet in Horn.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「彗星見兩角間色白者，軍起不戰，邦有大喪。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When a comet appears between the horns white, armies arise without pitched battle and the state meets great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: White horn comet brings bloodless war and state mourning.

sentences.zh: 」景元元年，高貴鄉公為成濟所害。

translations.literal: In Jingyuan 1 the Duke of Gaoguixiang fell to Cheng Ji’s assassins.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mao died at Cheng Ji’s hands.

sentences.zh: 四年十月丁丑，客星見太微中，轉東南行，歷軫宿，積七日滅。

translations.literal: On dingchou in the fourth year’s tenth month a guest star appeared inside the Supreme Palace, drifting southeast through Chariot, gone in seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Guest star crossed Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「客星出太微，有兵喪。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Guest stars from the Supreme Palace mean armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guest stars augur war.

translations.literal: In Jingyuan 1 the Duke of Gaoguixiang was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan 1 regicide.

sentences.zh: 元帝景元三年十一月壬寅，彗星見亢，色白，長五寸，轉北行，積四十五日滅。

translations.literal: On renyin in the third year of Emperor Yuan of Wei’s Jingyuan era eleventh month a comet appeared in Horn white five cun, turning north, fading after forty-five days.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jingyuan 3 comet in Horn.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning.

translations.literal: Another saying: “When a comet appears in Horn the Son of Heaven loses virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Horn comet indicts royal virtue.

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zhong Hui and Deng Ai conquered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Year four Shu fell.

translations.literal: Both generals rebelled and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Both met execution.

sentences.zh: 咸熙二年五月，彗星見王良，長丈餘，色白，東南指，積十二日滅。

translations.literal: In Xianxi 2 fifth month a comet appeared at Wangliang over one zhang white pointing southeast, gone in twelve days.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxi 2 May comet at Wangliang.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Wangliang is the Son of Heaven’s chariot team.
translations.idiomatic: Wangliang guides the royal chariot.

sentences.zh: 彗星掃之，禪代之表，除舊布新之象也。

translations.literal: When a comet sweeps it, tables foretell abdication—renewing the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Comet sweep means abdication omen.

translations.literal: White color means mourning.
translations.idiomatic: White comets signal mourning.

sentences.zh: 王良在東壁宿，又并州之分野。

translations.literal: Wangliang lies by Eastern Wall—in Bingzhou’s field.
translations.idiomatic: Wangliang ties to Bingzhou.

translations.literal: In the eighth month Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: August Emperor Wen (Cao Pi) died.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Emperor Wu received Wei’s abdication.
translations.idiomatic: December Sima Yan accepted Wei abdication.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始四年正月丙戌，彗星見軫，青白色，西北行，又轉東行。

translations.literal: On bingxu in Taishi 4 New Year a comet appeared in Chariot bluish-white moving northwest then east.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Taishi 4 comet in Chariot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪，軫又楚分野。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be armies and mourning; Chariot is Chu’s field.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot comet threatens Chu.

translations.literal: In the third month Empress Dowager Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: March buried Empress Dowager Wang.

translations.literal: In the tenth month Wu raided Jiangxia and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: October Wu struck Jiangxia.

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year a broom star trespassed Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year ninth month comet in Purple Palace.

translations.literal: The interpretation matches the foregoing.
translations.idiomatic: Same gloss.

translations.literal: Purple Forbidden is the Son of Heaven’s inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Purple Palace equals throne enclosure.

translations.literal: In the tenth year Empress Wu Yuan Yang died.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth year Yang empress died.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月，有星孛於軫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the tenth year a broom star appeared in Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth year December comet in Chariot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天下兵起，軫又楚分野。」

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Under Heaven armies arise; Chariot again marks Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide arms—Chariot is Chu.

sentences.zh: 咸寧二年六月甲戌，星孛於氐。

translations.literal: On jiaxu in Xianning 2 sixth month a broom star appeared at Base.
translations.idiomatic: Xianning 2 June comet at Base.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The Son of Heaven loses virtue and governance shifts.
translations.idiomatic: Loss of virtue transfers rule.

translations.literal: Base moreover marks Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Base equals Yanzhou.

translations.literal: In the seventh month a broom star appeared at Great Horn.
translations.idiomatic: July comet at Great Horn.

translations.literal: Great Horn is the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Great Horn is regnal seat.

sentences.zh: 八月，星孛太微，至翼、北斗、三台。

translations.literal: In the eighth month a broom star crossed Supreme Palace reaching Wings, Dipper, Three Steps.
translations.idiomatic: August comet through palace asterisms.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「太微，天子庭，大人惡之。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Supreme Palace is the Son of Heaven’s courtyard—great men dread it.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Palace alarms magnates.

translations.literal: Another saying: “There will be change of king.
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic turnover.

translations.literal: Wings again marks Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Wings is Chu.

sentences.zh: 北斗主殺罰，三台為三公。

translations.literal: The Dipper governs punishments; Three Steps are the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper sentences; Steps are dukes.

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month a broom star appeared in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Third year New Year western comet.

translations.literal: In the third month a broom star appeared in Stomach.
translations.idiomatic: March comet in Stomach.

translations.literal: Stomach marks Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Stomach matches Xuzhou.

translations.literal: In the fourth month a broom star struck Maid.
translations.idiomatic: April comet at Maid.

translations.literal: Maid governs the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Maid is harem.

translations.literal: In the fifth month another broom star appeared in the east.
translations.idiomatic: May eastern comet.

translations.literal: In the seventh month a broom star trespassed Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: July Purple Palace comet.

translations.literal: The superior gloss says: “Under Heaven the ruler will change.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven changes sovereign.

translations.literal: In the fourth year Chiyou’s banner appeared in Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year Chiyou banner in Well.

sentences.zh: 後二年，傾三方伐吳，是其應也。

translations.literal: Two years later the three-sided assault on Wu fulfilled it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu conquest matched omen.

translations.literal: In the fifth year’s third month a broom star appeared in Willow.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year March Willow comet.

translations.literal: In the fourth month another appeared at Maid.
translations.idiomatic: April Maid comet.

translations.literal: In the seventh month it trespassed Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: July Purple Palace comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Outer ministers bully their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Vassals overpower sovereign.

translations.literal: Willow marks Three Rivers field.
translations.idiomatic: Willow equals Three Rivers.

sentences.zh: 大角、太微、紫宮、女御並為王者。

translations.literal: Great Horn, Supreme Palace, Purple Forbidden, and Maid all image kings.
translations.idiomatic: Royal stars align.

translations.literal: The next year Wu perished—exactly its fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Wu fell.

translations.literal: Broom stars preside over armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Comets mean war deaths.

sentences.zh: 征吳之役，三河、徐、兗之兵悉出，交戰于吳楚之地，吳丞相都督以下梟戮十數，偏裨行陣之徒馘斬萬計，皆其徵也。

translations.literal: The Wu campaign mobilized Three Rivers, Xu, and Yanzhou troops clashing in Wu-Chu—Wu’s commanders decapitated by the dozen and tens of thousands slain in the ranks answered every sign.
translations.idiomatic: Conquest carnage matched every comet.

sentences.zh: 太康二年八月，有星孛于張。

translations.literal: In Taikang 2 eighth month a broom star appeared in Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang 2 August Zhang comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning.

translations.literal: In the eleventh month a broom star appeared at Zhan Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: November comet at execution cart.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The rear palace will answer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Harem bears sign.

translations.literal: On wushen in the fourth year’s third month a broom star appeared in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year March southwest comet.

sentences.zh: 是年，齊王攸、任城王陵、琅邪王伷、新都王該薨。

translations.literal: That year Prince You of Qi, Prince Ling of Rencheng, Prince Zhou of Langye, and Prince Gai of Xindu died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima You of Qi, Sima Ling of Rencheng, Sima Zhou of Langye, and Sima Gai of Xindu all died that year.

sentences.zh: 八年九月，星孛於南斗，長數十丈餘日滅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year a broom star appeared in Southern Dipper dozens of zhang long lasting many days.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth year ninth month Dipper comet.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「斗主爵祿，國有大憂。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The Dipper governs rank stipends—the state faces great sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper comet threatens salaries and throne.

sentences.zh: 」一曰：「孛于斗，王者疾病，天下易政，大亂兵起。」

translations.literal: Another saying: “A comet in the Dipper means royal illness, altered governance, and great rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper comet overturns rule.

sentences.zh: 太熙元年四月，客星在紫宮。

translations.literal: In Taixi 1 fourth month a guest star stood in Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Taixi 1 April guest star in Purple Palace.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning.

translations.literal: Near Taikang’s end Emperor Wu indulged feasting and fell chronically ill.
translations.idiomatic: Late Taikang Wu feasted into illness.

translations.literal: That month on jiyou the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou that month ended Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 永平元年，賈后誅楊駿及其黨與，皆夷三族，楊太后亦見弑。

translations.literal: In Yongping 1 Empress Jia executed Yang Jun and faction to third kin—even Empress Dowager Yang was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping purge slew Yang clan.

sentences.zh: 又誅汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋，王室兵喪之應也。

translations.literal: She also killed Prince Runan Liang, Grand Guardian Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—responses of martial mourning for the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Further kin slaughter followed.

sentences.zh: 惠帝元康五年四月，有星孛於奎，至軒轅、太微，經三台、太陵。

translations.literal: In Yuan-kang 5 fourth month a broom star appeared in Striding Legs reaching Chariot and Supreme Palace crossing Three Steps and Great Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan-kang 5 comet crossed capital stars.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「奎為魯，又為庫兵，軒轅為後宮，太微天子庭，三台為三司，太陵有積尸死喪之事。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Striding Legs is Lu and armory stores; Chariot Shaft is harem; Supreme Palace the court; Three Steps the Three Dukes; Great Mound holds piled corpses and death.
translations.idiomatic: Star labels map princes, harem, ministers.

translations.literal: Afterward the arsenal burned and Qiang rebelled west.
translations.idiomatic: Armory fire and Qiang revolt.

sentences.zh: 後五年，司空張華遇禍，賈后廢死，魯公賈謐誅。

translations.literal: Five years later Minister of Works Zhang Hua met disaster; Empress Jia was deposed and killed; Duke Lu Jia Mi executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Hua and Jia clan fell.

translations.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Sima Lun seized throne.

sentences.zh: 於是三王興兵討倫，兵士戰死十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Then the Three Princes rose against Lun—over a hundred thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Princely coalition slaughtered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 永康元年三月，妖星見南方。

translations.literal: In Yongkang 1 third month an evil star appeared in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Yongkang 1 March southern astral demon.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「妖星出，天下大兵將起。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When evil stars emerge great armies will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Demon stars mobilize hosts.

sentences.zh: 」是月賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺后，斬司空張華，又廢帝自立。

translations.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and murdered her, executed Zhang Hua, and enthroned himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jia killed heir; Lun purged court.

sentences.zh: 於是三王並起，迭總天權。

translations.literal: Then three princes rose, trading supreme authority.
translations.idiomatic: Princes vied for power.

sentences.zh: 其十二月，彗星出牽牛之西，指天市。

translations.literal: That twelfth month a comet emerged west of Herdsman pointing at Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: December comet Herdsman to market.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「牛者七政始，彗出之，改元易號之象也。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Ox begins the seven regulators; a comet there means changing era and reign title.
translations.idiomatic: Ox comet alters era names.

sentences.zh: 天市一名天府，一名天子旗，帝坐在其中。

translations.literal: Celestial Market is also called Celestial Treasury and Son of Heaven’s banner—the throne sits within.
translations.idiomatic: Market holds imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 」明年，趙王倫篡位，改元，尋為大兵所滅。

translations.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped, changed the era, then fell to great armies.
translations.idiomatic: Lun’s coup collapsed.

translations.literal: In the second year’s fourth month a comet appeared in Qi field.
translations.idiomatic: Year two April Qi comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Qi will suffer armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Qi faces war.

translations.literal: Then Prince Qi Jiong rose against Prince Zhao Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Qi prince attacked Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奢。

translations.literal: After Lun fell Jiong kept armies outside court, monopolizing power in arrogance and luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong tyrannized Luoyang.

translations.literal: The next year he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong executed next year.

sentences.zh: 太安元年四月，彗星晝見。

translations.literal: In Tai’an 1 fourth month a comet appeared by day.
translations.idiomatic: Tai’an 1 April daytime comet.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，彗星見東方，指三台。

translations.literal: In Tai’an 2 third month a comet appeared in the east pointing at Three Steps.
translations.idiomatic: Tai’an 2 March eastern comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Image of armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Martial mourning.

translations.literal: Three Steps mean Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Steps equal dukes.

sentences.zh: 」三年正月，東海王越執太尉、長沙王乂，張方又殺之。

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month Prince Donghai Yue seized Grand Commandant Prince Changsha Yi and Zhang Fang murdered him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue arrested Yi; Fang killed him.

sentences.zh: 永興元年五月，客星守畢。

translations.literal: In Yongxing 1 fifth month a guest star guarded the Net.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing 1 May guest star at Net.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The Son of Heaven will lack heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty loses heirs.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Great ministers will be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers executed.

sentences.zh: 」時諸王擁兵，其後惠帝失統，終無繼嗣。

translations.literal: At that time princes wielded arms; later Emperor Hui lost control and finally had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: Princely armies left Hui without heir.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，有星孛于昴畢。

translations.literal: In the second year’s eighth month a broom star appeared in Mao and Net.
translations.idiomatic: Year two August Mao-Net comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning.

translations.literal: Mao and Net again mark Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Mao-Net equals Zhao-Wei.

translations.literal: On dingchou in the tenth month a broom star appeared in Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: October Dingchou Dipper comet.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「琁璣更授，天子出走。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “The Dipper’s pearl will be reassigned—the Son of Heaven flees.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper comet exiles sovereign.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Strong states raise armies while feudatories vie for power.
translations.idiomatic: Warlord struggle.

translations.literal: Afterward princes exchanged blows—each omen matched.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince war answered sky.

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: Hui died next year.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸和四年七月，有星孛於西北，犯斗，二十三日滅。

translations.literal: In Xianhe 4 seventh month a broom star appeared northwest transgressing Dipper gone in twenty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe 4 July northwest comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be martial turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Military chaos.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，郭默殺江州刺史劉胤，荊州刺史陶侃討默，斬之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Guo Mo killed Inspector Liu Yin; Tao Kan campaigned and beheaded Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo fell to Tao Kan.

translations.literal: At that time Shi Le first styled himself king.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le claimed kingship.

sentences.zh: 咸康二年正月辛巳，彗星夕見西方，在奎。

translations.literal: On xinsi in Xiankang 2 New Year a comet appeared at dusk west in Striding Legs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang 2 New Year evening comet in Legs.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning.

translations.literal: Striding Legs also govern frontier troops.
translations.idiomatic: Legs signal borders.

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month Shi Jilong arrogated Heavenly Kingship.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu crowned Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 四年，石季龍伐慕容皝，不克。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Shi Jilong campaigned against Murong Huang unsuccessfully.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu failed vs Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 既退，皝追擊之，又破麻秋。

translations.literal: On retreat Huang pursued and crushed Ma Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang routed Ma Qiu.

translations.literal: Huang then acknowledged Jin suzerainty—fitting frontier warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Submission matched border omen.

sentences.zh: 六年二月庚辰，有星孛於太微。

translations.literal: On gengchen in the sixth year’s second month a broom star appeared in Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year February Supreme Palace comet.

translations.literal: In the seventh year’s third month Empress Du died.
translations.idiomatic: March Empress Du died.

sentences.zh: 康帝建元元年十一月六日，彗星見亢，長七尺，白色。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the eleventh month of Jianyuan 1 a comet appeared in Horn seven feet white.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan 1 November Horn comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Horn is court—presiding armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Horn comet strikes court.

translations.literal: In the second year Emperor Kang died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang died year two.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和五年十一月乙卯，彗星見於亢。

translations.literal: On yimao in Yonghe 5 eleventh month a comet appeared in Horn.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe 5 November Horn comet.

translations.literal: Its tail pointed west white one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tail west, white, one zhang.

sentences.zh: 六年正月丁丑，彗星又見於亢。

translations.literal: On dingchou in the sixth year’s first month a comet again appeared in Horn.
translations.idiomatic: Year six January Horn comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Armies and mourning; pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: War, grief, plague.

translations.literal: That fifth year’s eighth month Chu Pou’s northern expedition failed.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou lost north.

sentences.zh: 十一月，冉閔殺石遵，又盡殺胡十餘萬人，於是中土大亂。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Ran Min killed Shi Zun and slaughtered Hu beyond a hundred thousand—central plains dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min’s purge devastated north.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Chu Pou died.
translations.idiomatic: December Chu Pou died.

translations.literal: That year great pestilence raged.
translations.idiomatic: Plague swept the year.

sentences.zh: 升平二年五月丁亥，彗星出天船，在胃。

translations.literal: On dinghai in Shengping 2 fifth month a comet emerged from Celestial Boat in Stomach.
translations.idiomatic: Shengping 2 May comet from Boat.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Armies and mourning—renewing the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: War clears old order.

translations.literal: Emerging from Celestial Boat means outer tribes invade.
translations.idiomatic: Boat comet brings barbarians.

translations.literal: Another saying: “Great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Floods follow.

translations.literal: In the fourth year’s fifth month under Heaven great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Year five May floods.

translations.literal: In the fifth year Emperor Mu died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu died.

sentences.zh: 哀帝興甯元年八月，有星孛於角亢，入天市。

translations.literal: In Xingning 1 eighth month a broom star appeared at Horn and Neck entering Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: Xingning 1 August comet Horn to Market.

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Archive gloss: martial mourning.

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: Year three January empress died.

translations.literal: In the second month the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: February emperor died.

sentences.zh: 三月，慕容恪攻沒洛陽，沈勁等戰死。

translations.literal: In the third month Murong Ke seized Luoyang—Shen Jin and others fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke took Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 海西太和四年二月，客星見紫宮西垣，至七月乃滅。

translations.literal: In Taihe 4 second month of Haixi a guest star appeared at Purple Forbidden’s western wall lasting until July.
translations.idiomatic: Haixi Taihe 4 guest star western palace.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「客星守紫宮，臣弑主。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When guest stars guard Purple Forbidden ministers assassinate their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Guest stars mean regicide.

translations.literal: In the sixth year Huan Wen deposed the emperor as Duke of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen demoted emperor.

sentences.zh: 孝武甯康二年正月丁巳，有星孛於女虛，經氐、亢、角、軫、翼、張。

translations.literal: On dingsi in Ningkang 2 New Year a broom star appeared at Maid and Emptiness crossing Base, Horn, Chariot, Wings, Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ningkang 2 sweeping comet.

sentences.zh: 至三月丙戌，彗星，見於氐。

translations.literal: By third month bingxu another comet appeared at Base.
translations.idiomatic: March comet at Base.

sentences.zh: 九月丁丑，有星孛於天市。

translations.literal: On dingchou in the ninth month a broom star appeared at Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: September market comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning.

sentences.zh: 」太元元年七月，苻堅破涼州，虜張天錫。

translations.literal: In Taixuan 1 seventh month Fu Jian conquered Liangzhou and captured Zhang Tianxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian took Former Liang.

sentences.zh: 太元十一年三月，客星在南斗，至六月乃沒。

translations.literal: In Taixuan 11 third month a guest star stood in Southern Dipper until June.
translations.idiomatic: Taixuan 11 Dipper guest star.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be troops and amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Arms and pardon.

translations.literal: Afterward Si, Yong, Yan, and Ji constantly knew campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Heartland wars persisted.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月大赦，八月又大赦。

translations.literal: Twelfth year January great amnesty; August another.
translations.idiomatic: Two amnesties year twelve.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月壬申，有星孛於北河戍，經太微、三台、文昌，入北斗，色白，長十餘丈。

translations.literal: On renshen in the fifteenth year’s seventh month a broom star appeared at Northern River Guard crossing Supreme Palace, Three Steps, and Civilizing spanning Dipper white over ten zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Massive comet crossed court.

translations.literal: On wuxu in the eighth month it entered Purple Forbidden then vanished.
translations.idiomatic: August entered Purple Palace.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「北河戍一名胡門，胡有兵喪。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Northern River Guard is also Barbarian Gate—northern tribes suffer armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Guard star brings barbarian war.

sentences.zh: 掃太微，入紫微，王者當之。

translations.literal: Sweeping Supreme Palace into Purple Forbidden strikes the king.
translations.idiomatic: Comet threatens sovereign.

sentences.zh: 三台為三公，文昌為將相，將相三公有災。

translations.literal: Three Steps are Three Dukes; Civilizing governs generals and ministers—all suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers endangered.

translations.literal: Entering Dipper means feudatories executed.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper entry executes lords.

sentences.zh: 」一曰：「掃北斗，強國發兵，諸侯爭權，大人憂。

translations.literal: Another saying: “Sweeping Dipper makes strong states raise armies, feudatories contend, and great men grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper sweep ignites warlords.

translations.literal: Year twenty-one the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died in year twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 隆安元年，王恭、殷仲堪、桓玄等並發兵，表以誅王國寶為名。

translations.literal: In Long’an 1 Wang Gong, Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan and others all rose in arms, memorializing execution of Wang Guobao.
translations.idiomatic: Long’an 1 coalition demanded Wang Guobao’s head.

sentences.zh: 朝廷順而殺之，並斬其從弟緒，司馬道子由是失勢，禍亂成矣。

translations.literal: The court yielded, executed him and his cousin Xu, and Minister Daozi lost power—disaster ensued.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial compliance killed Guobao; chaos followed.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月，客星在尾中，至九月乃滅。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighteenth year a guest star remained in Tail until September.
translations.idiomatic: Year eighteen guest star in Tail.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Yan will have armies and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yan faces war and grief.

sentences.zh: 」二十年，慕容垂息寶伐魏，為所破，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Murong Bao, son of Chui, campaigned against Wei, was defeated, and tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao’s Wei campaign failed.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，垂死，國遂衰亡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Chui died and the state then declined to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Chui’s death ended Yan.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月，有蓬星如粉絮，東南行，歷女虛，至哭星。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twentieth year a broom star like powder-floss moved southeast through Girl and Emptiness to the Weepers.
translations.idiomatic: Broom star crossed north sky.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「蓬星見，不出三年，必有亂臣戮死於市。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When a broom star appears, within three years a traitor will be executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Broom star times regicide in market.

translations.literal: At that time Wang Guobao slandered the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao subverted court.

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-first year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor died year twenty-one September.

sentences.zh: 隆安元年，王恭等興兵，而朝廷殺王國寶、王緒。

translations.literal: In Long’an 1 Wang Gong and others raised arms while the court executed Wang Guobao and Wang Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Long’an opened with executions.

sentences.zh: 安帝隆安四年二月己丑，有星孛於奎，長三丈，上至閣道、紫宮西蕃，入北斗魁，至三台，三月，遂經於太微帝坐端門。

translations.literal: On jichou in the fourth year of Long’an a broom star appeared in Striding Legs three zhang long up to Censor Path and Supreme Palace’s western bastion, into Dipper’s handle, then Three Steps, and by the third month traversed the Supreme Palace throne and Portal Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Long’an 4 comet through palace stars.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「彗星掃天子庭閣道，易主之象。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Comets sweeping the court and Censor Path portend change of ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Comet at court means new sovereign.

translations.literal: It traversed Three Steps and entered the Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Comet crossed Three Steps and Dipper.

translations.literal: The interpretation matches the previous article.
translations.idiomatic: Same as prior entry.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊寅，有星孛于貫索、天市、天津。

translations.literal: On wuyin in the twelfth month a broom star appeared in Rope, Market, and Celestial Ford.
translations.idiomatic: December comet in market stars.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「貴臣獄死，內外有兵喪。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Noble ministers die in prison; interior and exterior know arms and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers jailed; war within and without.

sentences.zh: 天津為賊斷，王道天下不通。

translations.literal: Celestial Ford severed means bandits block the kingly way and all under Heaven cannot pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ford cut—roads closed.

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Calamity lies in Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Omen targets Wu-Yue.

sentences.zh: 」五年二月，有孫恩兵亂，攻侵郡國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year’s second month Sun En’s bands rioted, storming commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Year five Sun En uprising.

sentences.zh: 於是內外戒嚴，營陣屯守，柵斷淮口。

translations.literal: Interior and exterior armed; camps and stockades choked the Huai mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilization blocked Huai crossings.

sentences.zh: 九月，桓玄表至，逆旨陵上。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Huan Xuan’s memorial arrived impertinent and defiant.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan’s arrogant memorial.

sentences.zh: 其後玄遂篡位，亂京都，大饑，人相食，百姓流亡，皆其應也。

translations.literal: Afterward Xuan usurped, threw the capital into chaos, great famine, cannibalism, and mass exile—each omen matched.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan’s usurpation brought famine and flight.

sentences.zh: 元興元年十月，有客星色白如粉絮，在太微西，至十二月入太微。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Yuanxing 1 a guest star white as powder-floss sat west of the Supreme Palace, entering the palace by December.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing guest star into Supreme Palace.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Soldiers enter the Son of Heaven’s courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Troops invade court.

sentences.zh: 」二年十二月，桓玄篡位，放遷帝、后於尋陽，以永安何皇后為零陵君。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year Huan Xuan usurped, banished sovereign and empress to Xunyang, and demoted Empress He.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan exiled court.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，劉裕盡誅桓氏。

translations.literal: In the third year’s second month Liu Yu extirpated the Huans.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu wiped out Huans.

sentences.zh: 義熙十一年五月甲申，彗星二出天市，掃帝坐，在房心北。

translations.literal: On jiashen in the eleventh year of Yixi two comets emerged from Celestial Market sweeping the throne north of Room and Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Two comets swept throne stars.

translations.literal: Room and Heart mark Song’s field.
translations.idiomatic: Room-Heart govern Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 案占：「得彗柄者興，除舊布新，宋興之象。

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Whom the comet’s handle favors rises—purging old for new is Song’s omen.
translations.idiomatic: Handle toward Song meant Liu rise.

sentences.zh: 」十四年五月庚子，有星孛於北斗魁中。

translations.literal: On gengzi in the fourteenth year’s fifth month a broom star appeared inside Dipper’s handle.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth year May comet in Dipper.

sentences.zh: 七月癸亥，彗星出太微西，柄起上相星下，芒漸長至十餘丈，進掃北斗、紫微、中台。

translations.literal: On guihai in the seventh month a comet issued west of Supreme Palace from Upper Minister, tail lengthening ten zhang, sweeping Dipper, Purple Forbidden, and Central Step.
translations.idiomatic: July comet swept throne.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「彗出太微，社稷亡，天下易王；

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Comets from Supreme Palace mean altars fall and kings change.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Palace comet overturns dynasty.

translations.literal: Entering Dipper and Purple Forbidden empties the imperial palace.
translations.idiomatic: Comet hollows throne.

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Liu Yu returned to Pengcheng and took the Duke of Song investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu accepted Song dukedom.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor died December.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年正月戊戌，有星孛於太微西蕃。

translations.literal: On wuxu in Gongdi year one New Year a broom star appeared on Supreme Palace’s western bastion.
translations.idiomatic: Gongdi New Year comet.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Portent of dynastic revolution.
translations.idiomatic: Revolution sign.

translations.literal: That year Song possessed all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Song seized empire.

translations.literal: Shooting stars and meteor falls.
translations.idiomatic: Meteoric showers and falls.

sentences.zh: 蜀後主，諸葛亮帥大眾伐魏，屯于渭南。

translations.literal: The Later Lord of Shu led Zhuge Liang’s great host against Wei, camping south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shu invaded Wei south of Wei River.

sentences.zh: 有長星赤而芒角，自東北西南流，投亮營，三投再還，往大還小。

translations.literal: A long red star with horns moved northeast to southwest into Zhuge Liang’s camp—three times returning, shrinking each pass.
translations.idiomatic: Long red meteor struck Shu camp.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「兩軍相當，有大流星來走軍上及墜軍中者，皆破敗之徵也。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When armies face each other and great meteors fly over or into camps, both suffer defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Meteor over camp means rout.

sentences.zh: 」九月，亮卒於軍，焚營而退，群帥交怨，多相誅殘。

translations.literal: In September Zhuge Liang died in army; they burned camp and withdrew while commanders turned on one another.
translations.idiomatic: Liang died; Shu retreat chaotic.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝，宣帝圍公孫文懿于襄平。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei and Xuandi besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Wei besieged Yuan at Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 八月丙寅夜，有大流星長數十丈，白色有芒鬣，從首山東北流，墜襄平城東南。

translations.literal: On bingyin night in August a great meteor tens of zhang long white with maned tail flowed northeast from Mount Shou past Xiangping’s southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Meteor fell toward Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「圍城而有流星來走城上及墜城中者破。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “When besieging a city, meteors flying onto the walls or inside mean the city breaks.
translations.idiomatic: Meteor into siege breaks walls.

translations.literal: It also says: “Where stars fall becomes a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Fall site marks battle.

translations.literal: It also says: “Whatever land stars fall upon changes surname.
translations.idiomatic: Meteor fall changes dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」九月，文懿突圍走，至星墜所被斬，屠城，坑其眾。

translations.literal: In September Yuan broke out, fled to the fall site, was beheaded, the city slaughtered and buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan died at meteor site.

sentences.zh: 元帝六月，有大流星二並如斗，見西方，分流南北，光照地，隆隆有聲。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yuan’s sixth month two great meteors like dippers appeared west, splitting north and south, lighting earth with thunder rumble.
translations.idiomatic: Two grand meteors split sky.

sentences.zh: 案占：「流星為貴使，星大者使大。

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Meteors are noble envoys—the larger the star the greater the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Great meteors mean great missions.

sentences.zh: 」是年，鍾、鄧克蜀，二星蓋二帥之象。

translations.literal: That year Zhong and Deng conquered Shu—the two stars mirrored two commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Twin meteors matched two generals.

sentences.zh: 二帥相背，又分流南北之應。

translations.literal: Two commanders opposed each other—fitting north–south split.
translations.idiomatic: Split flow matched rivalry.

sentences.zh: 鍾會既叛，三軍憤怒，隆隆有聲，兵將怒之徵也。

translations.literal: After Zhong Hui rebelled three armies raged with thunder—noise of angry soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder echoed mutiny.

sentences.zh: 武帝七月，星隕如雨，皆西流。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu’s seventh month stars fell like rain—all westward.
translations.idiomatic: Wu seventh month meteor shower west.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Star falls mean commoners rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Meteor rain signals rebellion.

translations.literal: Westward flow meant Wu men submitting to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: West flow augured Wu surrender.

sentences.zh: 」二年，吳夏口督孫秀率部曲二千餘人來降。

translations.literal: In the second year Wu’s Xiakou commander Sun Xiu led over two thousand households to defect.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu defected to Jin.

translations.literal: On renzi in August stars fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: August meteor shower.

translations.literal: Liu Xiang’s tradition says: “Image of inferiors casting off superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Meteors mean subjects oust rulers.

sentences.zh: 」後三年，帝崩而惠帝立，天下自此亂矣。

translations.literal: Three years later the emperor died and Emperor Hui succeeded—under Heaven then slid into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Hui’s accession opened turmoil.

sentences.zh: 惠帝九月甲午，枉矢東北行，竟天。

translations.literal: On jiawu in Emperor Hui’s ninth month Crooked Arrow streaked northeast across the whole sky.
translations.idiomatic: Crooked Arrow crossed zenith.

sentences.zh: 六年六月丙午夜，有枉矢自斗魁東南行。

translations.literal: On bingwu midnight in the sixth year Crooked Arrow issued from Dipper handle southeastward.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year Crooked Arrow from Dipper.

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Chaos attacks chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Violence feasts on violence.

sentences.zh: 北斗主執殺，出斗魁，居中執殺者，不直之象也。

translations.literal: The Dipper governs executions; issuing from the handle means those wielding central killing power lack righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Handle arrow indicts unjust killers.

sentences.zh: 」是後，趙王殺張、裴，廢賈后，以理太子之冤，因自篡盜，以至屠滅，以亂伐亂之應也。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince Zhao slew Zhang and Pei, deposed Empress Jia to redress the heir—then seized power himself until extinction—chaos answering chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun’s purge mirrored omen.

sentences.zh: 一曰，氐帥齊萬年反之應也。

translations.literal: Another reading ties it to Di chieftain Qi Wannian’s rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate gloss: Qi Wannian.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛巳，有星晝隕中天北下，光變白，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On xinsi in the eleventh month a star daytime-fell north mid-sky turning white with thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Day bolide with thunder.

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Called Camp Leader.
translations.idiomatic: Named Camp Leader meteor.

sentences.zh: 營首所在，下有大兵，流血。

translations.literal: Where Camp Leader falls great armies spill blood below.
translations.idiomatic: Camp Leader brings blood.

sentences.zh: 」明年，劉元海、石勒攻略并州，多所殘滅。

translations.literal: The next year Liu Yuan and Shi Le ravaged Bingzhou with slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Le butchered Bing.

sentences.zh: 王浚起燕代，引鮮卑攻掠鄴中，百姓塗地。

translations.literal: Wang Jun rose in Yan-Dai leading Xianbei raids on Ye—people lay slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun’s raid devastated Hebei.

translations.literal: Thunder noise meant wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder signified rage.

translations.literal: On yichou in July stars fell with noise.
translations.idiomatic: July noisy meteor falls.

translations.literal: In the second year’s October stars again fell with noise.
translations.idiomatic: October repeat.

translations.literal: The interpretation matches the foregoing.
translations.idiomatic: Same gloss.

translations.literal: Afterward central Xia fell.
translations.idiomatic: Heartland fell.

translations.literal: In May Crooked Arrow flowed southwest.
translations.idiomatic: May southwest Crooked Arrow.

sentences.zh: 是時，司馬越西破河間兵，奉迎大駕，尋收繆胤、何綏等，肆無君之心，天下惡之。

translations.literal: At that time Sima Yue crushed Hejian forces westward, welcomed the imperial carriage, then seized Miao Yin and He Sui—heartless to his sovereign—and all under Heaven despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue’s arrogance matched omen.

sentences.zh: 及死而石勒焚其尸柩，是其應也。

translations.literal: When he died Shi Le burned his coffin—exact fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le burned Yue’s corpse.

sentences.zh: 懷帝九月辛卯，有大星如日，自西南流于東北，小者如斗，相隨，天盡赤，聲如雷。

translations.literal: On xinmao in Emperor Huai’s ninth month a star as bright as the sun flowed southwest to northeast; lesser stars like dippers followed—sky turned red with thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Huai’s reign saw giant bolide.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「流星為貴使，星大者使大。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Meteors are noble envoys—great stars mean great envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Large meteors equal great missions.

sentences.zh: 」是年五月，汲桑殺東燕王騰，遂據河北。

translations.literal: That May Ji Sang killed Prince Teng of Eastern Yan and seized Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang killed Sima Teng.

sentences.zh: 十一月，始遣和郁為征北將軍，鎮鄴西。

translations.literal: In November He Yu first dispatched north as general—stationed west of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Court posted He Yu north.

sentences.zh: 田甄等大破汲桑，斬于樂陵。

translations.literal: Tian Zhen crushed Ji Sang at Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhen slew Ji Sang.

sentences.zh: 於是以甄為汲郡太守，弟蘭钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: Zhen became Ji Administrator and brother Lan Julu prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen brothers rewarded.

sentences.zh: 小星相隨者，小將別帥之象也。

translations.literal: Lesser stars following meant lesser commanders’ omens.
translations.idiomatic: Small meteors minor leaders.

sentences.zh: 司馬越忿魏郡以東平原以南皆党于桑，以賞甄等，於是侵掠赤地。

translations.literal: Sima Yue resented Wei commandery east of Wei plain south allying with Sang—rewarded Zhen—then raided until land scorched.
translations.idiomatic: Yue’s reprisals ravaged plain.

translations.literal: Thunder noise signified rage.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder meant wrath.

sentences.zh: 四年十月庚子，大星西北墜，有聲。

translations.literal: On gengzi in the fourth year’s tenth month a great star fell northwest with noise.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year giant meteor.

translations.literal: Soon the emperor suffered shame at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor captured at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 元帝四月壬辰，枉矢出虛、危，沒翼、軫。

translations.literal: On renchen in Emperor Yuan’s fourth month Crooked Arrow issued from Emptiness and Rooftop vanishing in Wings and Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Crooked Arrow across lodges.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「枉矢所觸，天下之所伐。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Whatever Crooked Arrow strikes the realm campaigns against.
translations.idiomatic: Arrow marks target.

translations.literal: Wings and Chariot mark Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wings-Chariot equal Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 」，王敦殺譙王承及甘卓，而敦又梟夷，枉矢觸翼之應也。

translations.literal: Wang Dun slew Prince Cheng of Qiao and Gan Zhuo—then Dun himself extirpated—matching Arrow touching Wings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun’s fate tied to Wings.

sentences.zh: 七月甲午，有流星大如甕，長百餘丈，青赤色，從西方來，尾分為百餘岐，或散。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the seventh month there was a meteor as large as a jar, more than a hundred zhang long, blue-green and red in color; it came from the west, its tail split into more than a hundred forked trails, and in places dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the seventh month a meteor appeared, as large as a jar and over a hundred zhang long, tinged blue-green and red; it advanced from the west, and its tail divided into more than a hundred branching streaks, some of which scattered apart.

sentences.zh: 時王敦之亂，百姓流亡之應也。

translations.literal: It answered Wang Dun’s turmoil and mass exile.
translations.idiomatic: Meteor matched Dun revolt.

sentences.zh: 成帝元月辛末，流星大如二斗魁，色青赤，光耀地，出奎中，沒婁北。

translations.literal: On xinwei in Chengdi’s first month a meteor like two dipper bowls blue-green brilliant emerged from Striding Legs vanishing north of Bond.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe era meteor Striding Legs.

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Means famine—five grains unstored.
translations.idiomatic: Meteor forecasts famine.

translations.literal: That month great drought and famine.
translations.idiomatic: Drought that month.

sentences.zh: 六年二月庚午朔，有流星大如斗，光耀地，出天市，西行人太微。

translations.literal: On gengwu new moon in the sixth year’s second month a meteor like a dipper brilliant emerged from Celestial Market entering Supreme Palace west.
translations.idiomatic: Meteor Market to palace.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Great men will answer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Magnates bear sign.

translations.literal: In the eighth year’s sixth month Emperor Cheng died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng died.

sentences.zh: 穆帝六月辛巳，日未入，有流星大如三斗魁，從辰巳上，東南行。

translations.literal: On xinsi in Emperor Mu’s sixth month before sunset a meteor like three dippers moved southeast from chen-si hours.
translations.idiomatic: Mu reign afternoon meteor.

sentences.zh: 晷度推之，在箕、斗之間，蓋燕分也。

translations.literal: Shadow reckoning placed it between Winnowing Basket and Dipper—Yan field.
translations.idiomatic: Meteor in Yan sector.

translations.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Called Camp Leader.
translations.idiomatic: Named Camp Leader.

translations.literal: Beneath Camp Leader blood flows in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: Camp Leader bleeds land.

sentences.zh: 」是時，慕容雋僭稱大燕，攻伐無已。

translations.literal: Then Murong Jun styled Great Yan and campaigned endlessly.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun raided ceaselessly.

sentences.zh: 十年四月癸未，流星大如斗，色赤黃，出織女，沒造父，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On guiwei in the tenth year’s fourth month a meteor like a dipper red-yellow emerged from Weaving Maid vanishing at Zaofu with thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Large meteor Weaving to Zaofu.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「燕齊有兵，百姓流亡。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Yan and Qi have arms; commoners flee.
translations.idiomatic: Yan-Qi warfare.

sentences.zh: 」其年十二月，慕容雋遂據臨漳，盡有幽、并、青、冀之地。

translations.literal: That December Murong Jun seized Linzhang holding You, Bing, Qing, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jun conquered north.

sentences.zh: 緣河諸將奔散，河津隔絕。

translations.literal: River generals scattered; fords closed.
translations.idiomatic: River defenses collapsed.

translations.literal: Murong Ke attacked Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke struck Qi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，枉矢自東南流於西北，其長半天。

translations.literal: In November Crooked Arrow flowed southeast to northwest half the sky long.
translations.idiomatic: November long Crooked Arrow.

sentences.zh: 四年十月庚戌，天狗見西南。

translations.literal: On gengxu in the fourth year’s tenth month Celestial Dog appeared southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Dog in southwest.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Great warfare and flowing blood.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Dog means battle.

sentences.zh: 海西十月壬申，有大流星西下，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On renshen in Haixi tenth month a great meteor fell west with thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Haixi great meteor.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣使免袁真為庶人。

translations.literal: The next year envoys demoted Yuan Zhen to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen stripped.

sentences.zh: 桓溫在壽春，真病死，息瑾代立，求救於苻堅。

translations.literal: Huan Wen at Shouchun—Zhen died ill; son Jin succeeded seeking Fu Jian’s aid.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchun succession.

translations.literal: Wen defeated Fu Jian’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Wen beat Fu Jian.

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shouchun fell.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchun fell.

sentences.zh: 孝武十月乙卯，有奔星東南經翼、軫，聲如雷。

translations.literal: On yimao in Emperor Xiaowu’s tenth month a shooting star streaked southeast through Wings and Chariot with thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu meteor with thunder.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「楚地有兵，軍破，百姓流亡。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Chu will have arms—armies break and people flee.
translations.idiomatic: Chu warfare.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，苻堅荊州刺史梁成、襄陽太守閻震率眾伐竟陵，桓石虔擊大破之，生擒震，斬首七千，獲生口萬人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Fu Jian’s inspector of Jing Province Liang Cheng and Xiangyang prefect Yan Zhen led troops to attack Jingling; Huan Shiqian attacked them and inflicted a crushing defeat, capturing Yan Zhen alive, beheading seven thousand, and taking ten thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Liang Cheng, Fu Jian’s inspector of Jing Province, and Yan Zhen, prefect of Xiangyang, led their forces against Jingling. Huan Shiqian engaged them and broke them completely: he seized Yan Zhen alive, took seven thousand heads, and captured ten thousand people.

translations.literal: Thunder meant angry commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder signified commander wrath.

sentences.zh: 十三年閏月戊辰，天狗東北下，有聲。

translations.literal: On wuchen in intercalary month of the thirteenth year Celestial Dog fell northeast with noise.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Dog meteor.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Great battles and flowing blood.
translations.idiomatic: Great battle blood.

sentences.zh: 」自是後，慕容垂、翟遼、姚萇、苻登、慕容永並阻兵爭強。

translations.literal: Afterward Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, Murong Yong barricaded troops.
translations.idiomatic: Northern warlords contested.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，彭城妖賊又稱偽號於皇丘，劉牢之破滅之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year’s first month Pengcheng spirit-bandits styled a reign at Huangqiu until Liu Laozhi destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Huangqiu bandits fell.

sentences.zh: 三月，張道破合鄉、太山，向欽之擊走之。

translations.literal: In March Zhang Dao seized Hexiang and Taishan until Xiang Qinzhi repulsed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dao defeated.

sentences.zh: 安帝三月甲寅，流星赤色，眾多西行，經牽牛、虛、危、天津、閣道，貫太微、紫宮。

translations.literal: On jiayin in Emperor An’s third month red meteors numerous moved west through Herdsman, Emptiness, Celestial Ford, Censor Path into Supreme Palace and Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Red meteor storm crossed throne.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「星庶人類，眾多西行，眾將西流之象。

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Stars are masses—many westbound mean hosts drifting west.
translations.idiomatic: Mass western flow.

sentences.zh: 經天子庭，主弱臣強，諸侯兵不制。

translations.literal: Crossing court means weak sovereign and strong ministers—feudatories uncontrollable.
translations.idiomatic: Court crossing marks minister power.

sentences.zh: 」其年五月，孫恩侵吳郡，殺內史。

translations.literal: That May Sun En attacked Wu Commandery killing the governor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En struck Wu.

translations.literal: In June he reached Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: June reached Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 於是內外戒嚴，營陣屯守，劉裕追破之。

translations.literal: Interior and exterior armed while Liu Yu pursued and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu crushed Sun En.

sentences.zh: 元興元年七月，大饑，人相食。

translations.literal: In Yuanxing 1 seventh month great famine—people ate each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing famine cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 浙江以東流亡十六七，吳郡、吳興戶口減半，又流奔而西者萬計。

translations.literal: East of the Zhe River sixty or seventy percent of the people were displaced; in Wu Commandery and Wuxing registered households were halved; moreover those who fled westward numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Zhe River, six or seven people in ten were driven into exile; in Wu Commandery and Wuxing the population on the registers had fallen by half, and those who streamed westward to escape were counted in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 十月，桓玄遣將擊劉軌，破走之。

translations.literal: In October Huan Xuan sent generals against Liu Gui routing him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan struck Liu Gui.

translations.literal: Gui fled to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gui fled Qingzhou.

translations.literal: Cloud vapors.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud vapors.

sentences.zh: 惠帝十二月壬寅夜，有赤氣亙天，砰隱有聲。

translations.literal: On renyin night in Emperor Hui’s December red vapor bridged heaven with dull thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Red vapor spanning sky.

sentences.zh: 二年十月丁丑，赤氣見北方，東西竟天。

translations.literal: On dingchou in the second year’s tenth month red vapor appeared north spanning east–west.
translations.idiomatic: Northern red band.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Both mean great armies.
translations.idiomatic: Red mists mean war.

translations.literal: Dull thunder meant wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder anger.

translations.literal: Afterward the four seas churned and nine circuits fought.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide warfare.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲申，有白氣若虹，中天北下至地，夜見五日乃滅。

translations.literal: On jiashen in December white vapor like a rainbow hung north–south from zenith to earth five nights.
translations.idiomatic: White rainbow five nights.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Great armies arise.
translations.idiomatic: White rainbow armies.

sentences.zh: 」明年，王彌起青徐，汲桑亂河北，毒流天下。

translations.literal: The next year Wang Mi rose in Qing-Xu while Ji Sang ravaged Hebei—poison spread.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi and Ji Sang uprisings.

sentences.zh: 懷帝十一月乙亥，有白氣如帶，出南北方各二，起地至天，貫參伐中。

translations.literal: On yihai in Emperor Huai’s November white vapor like belts rose north and south from earth to heaven piercing Orion’s Battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cross belts through Orion.

translations.literal: The omen-text says: “Under Heaven great armies arise.
translations.idiomatic: Universal war.

translations.literal: In March of the fourth year Sima Yue seized Miao Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yue arrested Yin.

translations.literal: Moreover three fronts fought without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Tripartite war.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，司馬越死于甯平城，石勒攻破其眾，死者十餘萬人。

translations.literal: In March of the fifth year Sima Yue died at Ningping—Shi Le shattered his host—over a hundred thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Yue died at Ningping.

sentences.zh: 六月，京都焚滅，帝如虜庭。

translations.literal: In June the capital burned and the emperor went to barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang fell—emperor captive.

sentences.zh: 愍帝十月己巳夜，有赤氣曜於西北。

translations.literal: On jisi night in Emperor Min’s tenth month red vapor glowed northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Min reign red glow.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史陶侃討杜弢之党於石城，戰敗。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Tao Kan campaigned against Du Tao’s faction at Shicheng and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan lost at Shicheng.
